title.zh: 卷九十四 志第四十三: 食貨二
title.raw: 卷九十四 志第四十三: 食貨二 Volume 94 Treatises 47: Finance and Economics 2

sentences.zh: 食貨二 ○歲課

translations.literal: Finance and Economics II ○ Annual Levies
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics, Part Two — Annual Production Levies

sentences.zh: 山林川澤之產，若金、銀、珠、玉、銅、鐵、水銀、朱砂、碧甸子、鉛、錫、礬、硝、堿、竹、木之類，皆天地自然之利，有國者之所必資也，而或以病民者有之矣。

translations.literal: Products of mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes — such as gold, silver, pearls, jade, copper, iron, mercury, cinnabar, turquoise, lead, tin, alum, saltpeter, alkali, bamboo, and timber — are all natural benefits of heaven and earth, resources that any state must necessarily rely upon; yet there have been cases in which they have instead harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: The bounty of mountains, forests, rivers, and marshes—gold, silver, pearls, jade, copper, iron, mercury, cinnabar, turquoise, lead, tin, alum, saltpeter, alkali, bamboo, timber, and the like—are heaven's own gifts that every state must draw upon; and yet sometimes they have been turned into a burden upon the people.

sentences.zh: 元興，因土人呈獻，而定其歲入之課，多者不盡收，少者不強取，非知理財之道者，能若是乎？

translations.literal: When the Yuan rose to power, on the basis of what local people presented they fixed the annual levies due; where yield was great they did not take it all, where yield was slight they did not exact by force — could anyone who did not understand the way of managing finances have acted thus?
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Yuan, annual levies were set according to what local people reported; where production was abundant the state did not take everything, and where it was scant the state did not press for more. Could anyone ignorant of sound fiscal management have governed so wisely?

sentences.zh: 產金之所，在腹裏曰益都、檀、景，遼陽省曰大寧、開元，江浙省曰饒、徽、池、信，江西省曰龍興、撫州，湖廣省曰嶽、澧、沅、靖、辰、潭、武岡、寶慶，河南省曰江陵、襄陽，四川省曰成都、嘉定，雲南省曰威楚、麗江、大理、金齒、臨安、曲靖、元江、羅羅、會川、建昌、德昌、柏興、烏撒、東川、烏蒙。

translations.literal: Places where gold is produced: within the metropolitan region are Yidu, Tan, and Jing; in Liaoyang province are Daining and Kaiyuan; in Jiangzhe province are Rao, Hui, Chi, and Xin; in Jiangxi province are Longxing and Fuzhou; in Huguang province are Yue, Li, Yuan, Jing, Chen, Tan, Wugang, and Baoqing; in Henan province are Jiangling and Xiangyang; in Sichuan province are Chengdu and Jiaoding; in Yunnan province are Weichu, Lijiang, Dali, Jinchi, Lin'an, Qujing, Yuanjiang, Luoluo, Huichuan, Jianchang, Dechang, Baixing, Wusa, Dongchuan, and Wumeng.
translations.idiomatic: Gold was mined in the metropolitan districts of Yidu, Tan, and Jing; in Liaoyang at Daining and Kaiyuan; in Jiangzhe at Rao, Hui, Chi, and Xin; in Jiangxi at Longxing and Fuzhou; in Huguang at Yue, Li, Yuan, Jing, Chen, Tan, Wugang, and Baoqing; in Henan at Jiangling and Xiangyang; in Sichuan at Chengdu and Jiaoding; and in Yunnan at Weichu, Lijiang, Dali, Jinchi, Lin'an, Qujing, Yuanjiang, Luoluo, Huichuan, Jianchang, Dechang, Baixing, Wusa, Dongchuan, and Wumeng.

sentences.zh: 產銀之所，在腹裏曰大都、真定、保定、雲州、般陽、晉寧、懷孟、濟南、寧海，遼陽省曰大寧，江浙省曰處州、建寧、延平，江西省曰撫、瑞、韶，湖廣省曰興國、郴州，河南省曰汴梁、安豐、汝寧，陜西省曰商州，雲南省曰威楚、大理、金齒、臨安、元江。

translations.literal: Places where silver is produced: within the metropolitan region are Dadu, Zhending, Baoding, Yunzhou, Banyang, Jinning, Huaimeng, Jinan, and Ninghai; in Liaoyang province is Daining; in Jiangzhe province are Chuzhou, Jianning, and Yanping; in Jiangxi province are Fu, Rui, and Shao; in Huguang province are Xingguo and Chenzhou; in Henan province are Bianliang, Anfeng, and Runing; in Shaanxi province is Shangzhou; in Yunnan province are Weichu, Dali, Jinchi, Lin'an, and Yuanjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Silver was mined in the metropolitan region at Dadu, Zhending, Baoding, Yunzhou, Banyang, Jinning, Huaimeng, Jinan, and Ninghai; in Liaoyang at Daining; in Jiangzhe at Chuzhou, Jianning, and Yanping; in Jiangxi at Fu, Rui, and Shao; in Huguang at Xingguo and Chenzhou; in Henan at Bianliang, Anfeng, and Runing; in Shaanxi at Shangzhou; and in Yunnan at Weichu, Dali, Jinchi, Lin'an, and Yuanjiang.

sentences.zh: 產珠之所，曰大都，曰南京，曰羅羅，曰水達達，曰廣州。

translations.literal: Places where pearls are produced are Dadu, Nanjing, Luoluo, Shuidada, and Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pearls were gathered at Dadu, Nanjing, Luoluo, Shuidada, and Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 產玉之所，曰于闐，曰匪力沙。

translations.literal: Places where jade is produced are Yutian and Feilisha.
translations.idiomatic: Jade came from Yutian and Feilisha.

sentences.zh: 產銅之所，在腹裏曰益都，遼陽省曰大寧，雲南省曰大理、澄江。

translations.literal: Places where copper is produced: within the metropolitan region is Yidu; in Liaoyang province is Daining; in Yunnan province are Dali and Chengjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Copper was mined in the metropolitan district of Yidu, in Liaoyang at Daining, and in Yunnan at Dali and Chengjiang.

sentences.zh: 產鐵之所，在腹裏曰河東、順德、檀、景、濟南，江浙省曰饒、徽、寧國、信、慶元、臺、衢、處、建寧、興化、邵武、漳、福、泉，江西省曰龍興、吉安、撫、袁、瑞、贛、臨江、桂陽，湖廣省曰沅、潭、衡、武岡、寶慶、永、全、常寧、道州，陜西省曰興元，雲南省曰中慶、大理、金齒、臨安、曲靖、澄江、羅羅、建昌。

translations.literal: Places where iron is produced: within the metropolitan region are Hedong, Shunde, Tan, Jing, and Jinan; in Jiangzhe province are Rao, Hui, Ningguo, Xin, Qingyuan, Tai, Qu, Chu, Jianning, Xinghua, Shaowu, Zhang, Fu, and Quan; in Jiangxi province are Longxing, Ji'an, Fu, Yuan, Rui, Gan, Linjiang, and Guiyang; in Huguang province are Yuan, Tan, Heng, Wugang, Baoqing, Yong, Quan, Changning, and Daozhou; in Shaanxi province is Xingyuan; in Yunnan province are Zhongqing, Dali, Jinchi, Lin'an, Qujing, Chengjiang, Luoluo, and Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Iron was smelted in the metropolitan region at Hedong, Shunde, Tan, Jing, and Jinan; in Jiangzhe at Rao, Hui, Ningguo, Xin, Qingyuan, Tai, Qu, Chu, Jianning, Xinghua, Shaowu, Zhang, Fu, and Quan; in Jiangxi at Longxing, Ji'an, Fu, Yuan, Rui, Gan, Linjiang, and Guiyang; in Huguang at Yuan, Tan, Heng, Wugang, Baoqing, Yong, Quan, Changning, and Daozhou; in Shaanxi at Xingyuan; and in Yunnan at Zhongqing, Dali, Jinchi, Lin'an, Qujing, Chengjiang, Luoluo, and Jianchang.

sentences.zh: 產朱砂、水銀之所，在遼陽省曰北京，湖廣省曰沅、潭，四川省曰思州。

translations.literal: Places where cinnabar and mercury are produced: in Liaoyang province is Beijing; in Huguang province are Yuan and Tan; in Sichuan province is Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cinnabar and mercury came from Beijing in Liaoyang, from Yuan and Tan in Huguang, and from Sizhou in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 產碧甸子之所，曰和林，曰會川。

translations.literal: Places where turquoise is produced are Helin and Huichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Turquoise was mined at Helin and Huichuan.

sentences.zh: 產鉛、錫之所，在江浙省曰鉛山、臺、處、建寧、延平、邵武，江西省曰韶州、桂陽，湖廣省曰潭州。

translations.literal: Places where lead and tin are produced: in Jiangzhe province are Qianshan, Tai, Chu, Jianning, Yanping, and Shaowu; in Jiangxi province are Shaozhou and Guiyang; in Huguang province is Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lead and tin were mined in Jiangzhe at Qianshan, Tai, Chu, Jianning, Yanping, and Shaowu; in Jiangxi at Shaozhou and Guiyang; and in Huguang at Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 產礬之所，在腹裏曰廣平、冀寧，江浙省曰鉛山、邵武，湖廣省曰潭州，河南省曰廬州、河南。

translations.literal: Places where alum is produced: within the metropolitan region are Guangping and Jining; in Jiangzhe province are Qianshan and Shaowu; in Huguang province is Tanzhou; in Henan province are Luzhou and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Alum was produced in the metropolitan region at Guangping and Jining; in Jiangzhe at Qianshan and Shaowu; in Huguang at Tanzhou; and in Henan at Luzhou and Henan.

sentences.zh: 產硝、堿之所，曰晉寧。

translations.literal: The place where saltpeter and alkali are produced is Jinning.
translations.idiomatic: Saltpeter and alkali came from Jinning.

sentences.zh: 若竹、木之產，所在有之，不可以所言也。

translations.literal: As for the production of bamboo and timber, they exist everywhere and cannot all be enumerated.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo and timber, by contrast, were found nearly everywhere and cannot be listed in full.

sentences.zh: 初，金課之興，自世祖始。

translations.literal: At the outset, the establishment of the gold levy began with Emperor Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: The gold levy was first instituted under Emperor Shizu.

sentences.zh: 其在益都者，至元五年，命於從剛、高興宗以漏籍民戶四千，於登州棲霞縣淘焉。

translations.literal: As for that at Yidu, in the fifth year of Zhiyuan it was ordered that Yu Conggang and Gao Xingzong, with four thousand unregistered households, should pan for gold at Qixia county in Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Yidu, in Zhiyuan 5 (1268) Yu Conggang and Gao Xingzong were ordered to set four thousand unregistered households to panning gold at Qixia in Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，又以淘金戶二千簽軍者，付益都、淄萊等路淘金總管府，依舊淘金。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, two thousand gold-panning households who had been conscripted as soldiers were again assigned to the General Directorate of Gold Panning for the Yidu, Zilai, and other circuits, to pan for gold as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 15 (1278) another two thousand gold-panning households, previously conscripted as soldiers, were reassigned to the General Directorate of Gold Panning for Yidu, Zilai, and other circuits to resume panning.

sentences.zh: 其課於太府監輸納。

translations.literal: Their levy was delivered to the Directorate of the Palace Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: The levy was paid in to the Directorate of the Palace Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 在遼陽者，至元十年，聽李德仁於龍山縣胡碧峪淘采，每歲納課金三兩。

translations.literal: As for that in Liaoyang, in the tenth year of Zhiyuan Li Deren was permitted to pan and mine at Hubi Valley in Longshan county, paying three taels of gold in levy each year.
translations.idiomatic: In Liaoyang, Zhiyuan 10 (1273) Li Deren was allowed to work Hubi Valley in Longshan, paying an annual levy of three taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 十三年，又於遼東雙城及和州等處采焉。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, mining was also carried out at Shuangcheng and Hezhou and other places in eastern Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 13 (1276) mining was extended to Shuangcheng, Hezhou, and other sites in eastern Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 在江浙者，至元二十四年，立提舉司，以建康等處淘金夫凡七千三百六十五戶隸之，所轄金場凡七十餘所。

translations.literal: As for that in Jiangzhe, in the twenty-fourth year of Zhiyuan an Intendant Office was established, with a total of seven thousand three hundred sixty-five gold-panning households from Jiankang and other places placed under it, governing more than seventy gold fields.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangzhe, Zhiyuan 24 (1287) an Intendant Office was set up over 7,365 gold-panning households from Jiankang and elsewhere, overseeing more than seventy gold fields.

sentences.zh: 未幾以建康無金，革提舉司，罷淘金戶，其徽、饒、池、信之課，皆歸之有司。

translations.literal: Before long, because Jiankang had no gold, the Intendant Office was abolished and the gold-panning households dismissed; the levies from Hui, Rao, Chi, and Xin all reverted to the regular offices.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, when Jiankang proved barren of gold, the Intendant Office was abolished and the panning households disbanded; levies from Hui, Rao, Chi, and Xin were restored to the regular provincial administration.

sentences.zh: 在江西者，至元二十三年，撫州樂安縣小曹周歲辦金一百兩。

translations.literal: As for that in Jiangxi, in the twenty-third year of Zhiyuan Xiaocao in Le'an county, Fuzhou, furnished one hundred taels of gold per year.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi, Zhiyuan 23 (1286) Xiaocao in Le'an, Fuzhou, was assessed one hundred taels of gold annually.

sentences.zh: 在湖廣者，至元二十年，撥常德、澧、辰、沅、靖民萬戶，付金場轉運司淘焉。

translations.literal: As for that in Huguang, in the twentieth year of Zhiyuan ten thousand households from Changde, Li, Chen, Yuan, and Jing were allocated to the Gold Field Transport Commission for panning.
translations.idiomatic: In Huguang, Zhiyuan 20 (1283) ten thousand households from Changde, Li, Chen, Yuan, and Jing were assigned to the Gold Field Transport Commission for panning.

sentences.zh: 在四川者，元貞元年，以其病民罷之。

translations.literal: As for that in Sichuan, in the first year of Yuanzhen it was abolished because it harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan the levy was abolished in Yuanzhen 1 (1295) as an undue burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 在雲南者，至元十四年，諸路總納金一百五錠。

translations.literal: As for that in Yunnan, in the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan all circuits together paid in one hundred five ingots of gold.
translations.idiomatic: In Yunnan, Zhiyuan 14 (1277) all circuits together paid 105 ingots of gold.

sentences.zh: 此金課之興革可考者然也。

translations.literal: Such are the establishings and abolishings of the gold levy that can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the recorded establishments and abolitions of the gold levy.

sentences.zh: 銀在大都者，至元十一年，聽王庭璧於檀州奉先等洞采之。

translations.literal: As for silver at Dadu, in the eleventh year of Zhiyuan Wang Tingbi was permitted to mine at Fengxian and other caves in Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Dadu, Zhiyuan 11 (1274) Wang Tingbi was licensed to mine Fengxian and other caves in Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十五年，令關世顯等於薊州豐山采之。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Guan Shixian and others were ordered to mine at Fengshan in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 15 (1278) Guan Shixian and others were ordered to work Fengshan in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 在雲州者，至元二十七年，撥民戶於望雲煽煉，設從七品官掌之。

translations.literal: As for that in Yunzhou, in the twenty-seventh year of Zhiyuan civilian households were allocated to smelt at Wangyun, and a seventh-rank official was appointed to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: At Yunzhou, Zhiyuan 27 (1290) civilian households were assigned to smelt silver at Wangyun under a seventh-rank supervisor.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，又開聚陽山銀場。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the Juyangshan silver field was also opened.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 28 (1291) the Juyangshan silver field was also opened.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，遂立雲州等處銀場提舉司。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the Intendant Office for Silver Fields in Yunzhou and other places was then established.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 29 (1292) an Intendant Office for Silver Fields in Yunzhou and elsewhere was established.

sentences.zh: 在遼陽者，延祐四年，惠州銀洞三十六眼，立提舉司辦課。

translations.literal: As for that in Liaoyang, in the fourth year of Yanyou the thirty-six adits of the Huizhou silver mine were placed under an Intendant Office to handle the levy.
translations.idiomatic: In Liaoyang, Yanyou 4 (1317) the thirty-six adits of the Huizhou silver mine were placed under an Intendant Office to collect the levy.

sentences.zh: 在江浙者，至元二十一年，建寧南劍等處立銀場提舉司煽煉。

translations.literal: As for that in Jiangzhe, in the twenty-first year of Zhiyuan an Intendant Office for Silver Fields was established in Jianning, Nanjian, and other places for smelting.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangzhe, Zhiyuan 21 (1284) an Intendant Office for Silver Fields was set up in Jianning, Nanjian, and elsewhere to oversee smelting.

sentences.zh: 在湖廣者，至元二十三年，韶州路曲江縣銀場聽民煽煉，每年輸銀三千兩。

translations.literal: As for that in Huguang, in the twenty-third year of Zhiyuan the silver field at Qujiang county, Shaozhou circuit, permitted the people to smelt, paying three thousand taels of silver to the state each year.
translations.idiomatic: In Huguang, Zhiyuan 23 (1286) the Qujiang silver field in Shaozhou was opened to private smelting on an annual tribute of three thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 在河南者，延祐三年，李允直包羅山縣銀場，課銀三錠。

translations.literal: As for that in Henan, in the third year of Yanyou Li Yunzhi contracted for the Luoshan county silver field, with a levy of three ingots of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan, Yanyou 3 (1316) Li Yunzhi took contract for the Luoshan silver field at a levy of three ingots.

sentences.zh: 四年，李珪等包霍丘縣豹子崖銀洞，課銀三十錠，其所得礦，大抵以十分之三輸官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Li Gui and others contracted for the Baoziya silver cave in Huoqiu county, with a levy of thirty ingots; of ore obtained, roughly three-tenths were delivered to the government.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 4 (1317) Li Gui and others contracted for Baoziya in Huoqiu at thirty ingots, with roughly three-tenths of all ore yielded to the state.

sentences.zh: 此銀課之興革可考者然也。

translations.literal: Such are the establishings and abolishings of the silver levy that can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the recorded establishments and abolitions of the silver levy.

sentences.zh: 珠在大都者，元貞元年，聽民於楊村、直沽口撈采，命官買之。

translations.literal: As for pearls at Dadu, in the first year of Yuanzhen the people were permitted to dredge at Yangcun and Zhigukou, and officials were ordered to purchase them.
translations.idiomatic: At Dadu, Yuanzhen 1 (1295) the public was allowed to dredge pearls at Yangcun and Zhigukou, with mandatory sale to the government.

sentences.zh: 在南京者，至元十一年，命滅怯、安山等於宋阿江、阿爺苦江、忽呂古江采之。

translations.literal: As for that at Nanjing, in the eleventh year of Zhiyuan Mieqie, Anshan, and others were ordered to gather pearls at the Song'a River, the A'ye'ku River, and the Hulugu River.
translations.idiomatic: At Nanjing, Zhiyuan 11 (1274) Mieqie, Anshan, and others were ordered to gather pearls on the Song'a, A'ye'ku, and Hulugu rivers.

sentences.zh: 在廣州者，采於大步海。

translations.literal: As for that at Guangzhou, pearls were gathered in the Dabu Sea.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangzhou pearls were gathered in the Dabu Sea.

sentences.zh: 他如兀難、曲朵剌、渾都忽三河之珠，至元五年，徙鳳哥等戶撈焉。

translations.literal: Elsewhere, pearls of the Wunan, Quduola, and Hunduhu Three Rivers — in the fifth year of Zhiyuan households of Fengge and others were relocated to dredge for them.
translations.idiomatic: Pearls from the Wunan, Quduola, and Hunduhu rivers were dredged by households of Fengge and others relocated there in Zhiyuan 5 (1268).

sentences.zh: 勝州、延州、乃延等城之珠，十三年，命朵魯不<角┦>等撈焉。

translations.literal: Pearls of Shengzhou, Yanzhou, Naiyan, and other cities — in the thirteenth year Duolubu and others were ordered to dredge for them.
translations.idiomatic: Pearls from Shengzhou, Yanzhou, Naiyan, and other cities were dredged by Duolubu and others ordered to the task in Zhiyuan 13 (1276).

sentences.zh: 此珠課之興革可考者然也。

translations.literal: Such are the establishings and abolishings of the pearl levy that can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the recorded establishments and abolitions of the pearl levy.

sentences.zh: 玉在匪力沙者，至元十一年，迷兒、麻合馬、阿裏三人言，淘玉之戶舊有三百，經亂散亡，存者止七十戶，其力不充，而匪力沙之地旁近有民戶六十，每同淘焉。

translations.literal: As for jade at Feilisha, in the eleventh year of Zhiyuan Mir, Mahema, and Ali the three reported: formerly there were three hundred jade-washing households; through the turmoil they scattered and perished, and only seventy households remained — their strength was insufficient — yet near Feilisha there were sixty civilian households who washed jade together with them.
translations.idiomatic: At Feilisha, Zhiyuan 11 (1274) Mir, Mahema, and Ali reported that of three hundred jade-washing households only seventy survived the turmoil—too few to meet demand—while sixty nearby civilians regularly washed jade alongside them.

sentences.zh: 於是免其差徭，與淘戶等所淘之玉，於忽都、勝忽兒、舍裏甫丁三人所立水站，遞至京師。

translations.literal: Thereupon their corvée and tax obligations were remitted; jade washed by them together with the washing households was relayed to the capital by the water stations established by Hudu, Shenghu'er, and Sheli'fuding.
translations.idiomatic: Their corvée and tax duties were then remitted, and jade they washed with the licensed washers was relayed to the capital via water stations established by Hudu, Shenghu'er, and Sheli'fuding.

sentences.zh: 此玉課之興革可考者然也。

translations.literal: Such are the establishings and abolishings of the jade levy that can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the recorded establishments and abolitions of the jade levy.

sentences.zh: 銅在益都者，至元十六年，撥戶一千，於臨朐縣七寶山等處采之。

translations.literal: As for copper at Yidu, in the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan one thousand households were allocated to mine at Qibaoshan and other places in Linqu county.
translations.idiomatic: At Yidu, Zhiyuan 16 (1279) one thousand households were assigned to mine Qibaoshan and other sites in Linqu.

sentences.zh: 在遼陽者，至元十五年，撥采木夫一千戶，於錦、瑞州雞山、巴山等處采之。

translations.literal: As for that in Liaoyang, in the fifteenth year of Zhiyuan one thousand timber-gathering households were allocated to mine at Jishan and Bashan and other places in Jin and Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Liaoyang, Zhiyuan 15 (1278) one thousand timber-gathering households were reassigned to mine Jishan, Bashan, and other sites in Jin and Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 在澄江者，至元二十二年，撥漏籍戶於薩矣山煽煉，凡一十有一所。

translations.literal: As for that in Chengjiang, in the twenty-second year of Zhiyuan unregistered households were allocated to smelt at Sayishan, altogether eleven sites.
translations.idiomatic: At Chengjiang, Zhiyuan 22 (1285) unregistered households were set to smelt at Sayishan at eleven furnaces in all.

sentences.zh: 此銅課之興革可考者然也。

translations.literal: Such are the establishings and abolishings of the copper levy that can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the recorded establishments and abolitions of the copper levy.

sentences.zh: 鐵在河東者，太宗丙申年，立爐於西京州縣，撥冶戶七百六十煽焉。

translations.literal: As for iron at Hedong, in the bingshen year of Taizong furnaces were established in the prefectures and counties of Xijing, and seven hundred sixty smelting households were allocated to operate them.
translations.idiomatic: At Hedong, in Taizong's bingshen year (1236) furnaces were set up in the Xijing prefectures and counties with 760 smelting households assigned to run them.

sentences.zh: 丁酉年，立爐於交城縣，撥冶戶一千煽焉。

translations.literal: In the dingyou year furnaces were established in Jiaocheng county, and one thousand smelting households were allocated to operate them.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingyou year (1237) furnaces were set up in Jiaocheng with 1,000 smelting households.

sentences.zh: 至元五年，始立洞冶總管府。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan the General Directorate of Mining and Smelting was first established.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 5 (1268) the General Directorate of Mining and Smelting was first established.

sentences.zh: 七年罷之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished in Zhiyuan 7 (1270).

sentences.zh: 十三年，立平陽等路提舉司。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year an Intendant Office for the Pingyang and other circuits was established.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 13 (1276) an Intendant Office for Pingyang and other circuits was established.

sentences.zh: 十四年又罷之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year it was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished again in Zhiyuan 14 (1277).

sentences.zh: 其後廢置不常。

translations.literal: Thereafter it was established and abolished without fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter offices were established and abolished with no fixed pattern.

sentences.zh: 大德十一年，聽民煽煉，官為抽分。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade the people were permitted to smelt, and the government took a share.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 11 (1307) private smelting was permitted with the state taking a share.

sentences.zh: 至武宗至大元年，復立河東都提舉司掌之。

translations.literal: By the first year of Zhida under Emperor Wuzong, the Metropolitan Intendant Office of Hedong was re-established to administer it.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 1 (1308) under Emperor Wuzong the Metropolitan Intendant Office of Hedong was re-established to oversee it.

sentences.zh: 所隸之冶八：曰大通，曰興國，曰惠民，曰利國，曰益國，曰閏富，曰豐寧，豐寧之冶蓋有二云。

translations.literal: The smelteries under its jurisdiction were eight: called Datong, Xingguo, Huimin, Liguo, Yiguo, Runfu, and Fengning — the Fengning smelteries were in fact two.
translations.idiomatic: It oversaw eight smelteries: Datong, Xingguo, Huimin, Liguo, Yiguo, Runfu, and Fengning — the last name covering two furnaces.

sentences.zh: 在順德等處者，至元三十一年，撥冶戶六千煽焉。

translations.literal: As for that in Shunde and other places, in the thirty-first year of Zhiyuan six thousand smelting households were allocated to operate furnaces.
translations.idiomatic: At Shunde and elsewhere, Zhiyuan 31 (1294) six thousand smelting households were assigned to the furnaces.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，設都提舉司掌之，其後亦廢置不常。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade a Metropolitan Intendant Office was established to administer it; thereafter it too was established and abolished without fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 1 (1297) a metropolitan intendant office was set up; it too was later established and abolished irregularly.

sentences.zh: 至延祐六年，始罷兩提舉司，並為順德廣平彰德等處提舉司。

translations.literal: By the sixth year of Yanyou the two Intendant Offices were first abolished and merged into the Intendant Office for Shunde, Guangping, Zhangde, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 6 (1319) the two intendant offices were merged into one for Shunde, Guangping, Zhangde, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 所隸之冶六：曰神德，曰左村，曰豐陽，曰臨水，曰沙窩，曰固鎮。

translations.literal: The smelteries under its jurisdiction were six: called Shende, Zuocun, Fengyang, Linshui, Shawo, and Guzhen.
translations.idiomatic: It oversaw six smelteries: Shende, Zuocun, Fengyang, Linshui, Shawo, and Guzhen.

sentences.zh: 在檀、景等處者，太宗丙申年，始於北京撥戶煽焉。

translations.literal: As for that in Tan, Jing, and other places, in the bingshen year of Taizong households were first allocated from the Northern Capital to smelt.
translations.idiomatic: At Tan, Jing, and elsewhere, Taizong's bingshen year (1236) first saw households from the Northern Capital assigned to smelt iron.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，立提舉司掌之，其後亦廢置不常。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong an Intendant Office was established to administer it; thereafter it too was established and abolished without fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 2 (1261) an intendant office was established; it too was later established and abolished irregularly.

sentences.zh: 大德五年，始並檀、景三提舉司為都提舉司，所隸之冶有七：曰雙峰，曰暗峪，曰銀崖，曰大峪，曰五峪，曰利貞，曰錐山。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dade the three Intendant Offices of Tan and Jing were first merged into a Metropolitan Intendant Office; the smelteries under its jurisdiction were seven: called Shuangfeng, Anyu, Yinya, Dayu, Wuyu, Lizhen, and Zhuishan.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 5 (1301) the three Tan and Jing intendant offices were merged into one metropolitan office overseeing seven smelteries: Shuangfeng, Anyu, Yinya, Dayu, Wuyu, Lizhen, and Zhuishan.

sentences.zh: 在濟南等處者，中統四年，拘漏籍戶三千煽焉。

translations.literal: As for that in Jinan and other places, in the fourth year of Zhongtong three thousand unregistered households were seized to smelt.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinan and elsewhere, Zhongtong 4 (1263) three thousand unregistered households were conscripted to smelt.

sentences.zh: 至元五年，立洞冶總管府，其後亦廢置不常。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan the General Directorate of Mining and Smelting was established; thereafter it too was established and abolished without fixed pattern.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 5 (1268) the General Directorate of Mining and Smelting was set up; it too was later established and abolished irregularly.

sentences.zh: 至至大元年，復立濟南都提舉司，所隸之監有五：曰寶成，曰通和，曰昆吾，曰元國，曰富國。

translations.literal: By the first year of Zhida the Metropolitan Intendant Office of Jinan was re-established; the directorates under its jurisdiction were five: called Baocheng, Tonghe, Kunwu, Yuanguo, and Fuguo.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 1 (1308) the Metropolitan Intendant Office of Jinan was re-established, overseeing five directorates: Baocheng, Tonghe, Kunwu, Yuanguo, and Fuguo.

sentences.zh: 其在各省者，獨江浙、江西、湖廣之課為最多。

translations.literal: As for that in the various provinces, only the levies of Jiangzhe, Jiangxi, and Huguang were the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: Among the provinces, Jiangzhe, Jiangxi, and Huguang alone bore the heaviest iron levies.

sentences.zh: 凡鐵之等不一，有生黃鐵，有生青鐵，有青瓜鐵，有簡鐵，每引二百斤。

translations.literal: The grades of iron were not uniform: there was raw yellow iron, raw green iron, green-melon iron, and rod iron; each permit was for two hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: Iron came in several grades—raw yellow iron, raw green iron, green-melon iron, and rod iron—each transport permit covering two hundred jin.

sentences.zh: 此鐵課之興革可考者然也。

translations.literal: Such are the establishings and abolishings of the iron levy that can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the recorded establishments and abolitions of the iron levy.

sentences.zh: 朱砂、水銀在北京者，至元十一年，命蒙古都喜以恤品人戶於吉思迷之地采煉。

translations.literal: As for cinnabar and mercury in Beijing, in the eleventh year of Zhiyuan Menggu Duxi was ordered, with relief-supply households, to mine and smelt in the land of Jisim.
translations.idiomatic: At Beijing, Zhiyuan 11 (1274) Menggu Duxi was ordered, using relief-supply households, to mine and smelt cinnabar and mercury in Jisim.

sentences.zh: 在湖廣者，沅州五寨蕭雷發等每年包納朱砂一千五百兩，羅管賽包納水銀二千二百四十兩。

translations.literal: As for that in Huguang, Xiao Leifa and others of the Five Stockades of Yuanzhou contracted annually for one thousand five hundred taels of cinnabar, and Luoguansai for two thousand two hundred forty taels of mercury.
translations.idiomatic: In Huguang, Xiao Leifa and others of Yuanzhou's Five Stockades contracted for 1,500 taels of cinnabar yearly, and Luoguansai for 2,240 taels of mercury.

sentences.zh: 潭州安化縣每年辦朱砂八十兩、水銀五十兩。

translations.literal: Anhua county in Tanzhou furnished eighty taels of cinnabar and fifty taels of mercury each year.
translations.idiomatic: Anhua in Tanzhou furnished eighty taels of cinnabar and fifty of mercury annually.

sentences.zh: 碧甸子在和林者，至元十年，命烏馬兒采之。

translations.literal: As for turquoise at Helin, in the tenth year of Zhiyuan Wuma'er was ordered to mine it.
translations.idiomatic: At Helin, Zhiyuan 10 (1273) Wuma'er was ordered to mine turquoise.

sentences.zh: 在會川者，二十一年，輸一千餘塊。

translations.literal: As for that at Huichuan, in the twenty-first year more than one thousand blocks were delivered.
translations.idiomatic: At Huichuan, Zhiyuan 21 (1284) more than one thousand blocks were delivered.

sentences.zh: 此朱砂、水銀、碧甸子課之興革可考者然也。

translations.literal: Such are the establishings and abolishings of the cinnabar, mercury, and turquoise levies that can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the recorded establishments and abolitions of the cinnabar, mercury, and turquoise levies.

sentences.zh: 鉛、錫在湖廣者，至元八年，辰、沅、靖等處轉運司印造錫引，每引計錫一百斤，官收鈔三百文，客商買引，赴各冶支錫販賣。

translations.literal: As for lead and tin in Huguang, in the eighth year of Zhiyuan the Transport Commission of Chen, Yuan, Jing, and other places printed tin permits; each permit was for one hundred jin of tin, the government collecting three hundred cash in paper notes; merchants purchased permits and went to the various smelteries to draw tin for sale.
translations.idiomatic: In Huguang, Zhiyuan 8 (1271) the Chen, Yuan, and Jing Transport Commission issued tin permits of one hundred jin each at three hundred cash; merchants bought permits and drew tin from smelteries for resale.

sentences.zh: 無引者，比私鹽減等杖六十，其錫沒官。

translations.literal: Those without permits were, by comparison with illicit salt at reduced grade, beaten sixty strokes with the staff, and their tin was confiscated by the government.
translations.idiomatic: Those without permits were punished one grade below illicit salt—sixty strokes of the staff—and their tin confiscated.

sentences.zh: 此鉛、錫課之興革可考者然也。

translations.literal: Such are the establishings and abolishings of the lead and tin levies that can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the recorded establishments and abolitions of the lead and tin levies.

sentences.zh: 礬在廣平者，至元二十八年，路鵬舉獻磁州武安縣礬窯一十所，周歲辦白礬三千斤。

translations.literal: As for alum in Guangping, in the twenty-eighth year of Zhiyuan Lu Peng presented ten alum kilns in Wu'an county, Cizhou, furnishing three thousand jin of white alum per year.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangping, Zhiyuan 28 (1291) Lu Peng presented ten alum kilns in Wu'an, Cizhou, assessed at three thousand jin of white alum yearly.

sentences.zh: 在潭州者，至元十八年，李日新自具工本，於瀏陽永興礬場煎烹，每十斤官抽其二。

translations.literal: As for that in Tanzhou, in the eighteenth year of Zhiyuan Li Rixin provided his own capital and boiled alum at the Yongxing alum field in Liuyang; for every ten jin the government took two.
translations.idiomatic: In Tanzhou, Zhiyuan 18 (1281) Li Rixin financed boiling at Yongxing in Liuyang, the state taking two jin in every ten.

sentences.zh: 在河南者，二十四年，立礬課所於無為路，每礬一引重三十斤，價鈔五兩。

translations.literal: As for that in Henan, in the twenty-fourth year an Alum Levy Office was established on the Wuwei circuit; each alum permit was for thirty jin, priced at five taels in paper notes.
translations.idiomatic: In Henan, Zhiyuan 24 (1287) an Alum Levy Office was set up on the Wuwei circuit; each thirty-jin permit sold for five taels in paper notes.

sentences.zh: 此礬課之興革可考者然也。

translations.literal: Such are the establishings and abolishings of the alum levy that can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the recorded establishments and abolitions of the alum levy.

sentences.zh: 竹之所產雖不一，而腹裏之河南、懷孟，陜西之京兆、鳳翔，皆有在官竹園。

translations.literal: Although the places where bamboo is produced are not uniform, within the metropolitan region Henan and Huaimeng, and in Shaanxi Jingzhao and Fengxiang, all had government bamboo groves.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo grew in many places, but the metropolitan circuits of Henan and Huaimeng and the Shaanxi circuits of Jingzhao and Fengxiang all maintained government bamboo groves.

sentences.zh: 國初，皆立司竹監掌之，每歲令稅課所官以時采斫，定其價為三等，易於民間。

translations.literal: At the founding of the dynasty, Bamboo Directorates were established in each place to administer them; each year officials of the tax offices were ordered to harvest at the proper season, fix prices in three grades, and exchange with the populace.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding Bamboo Directorates were set up everywhere; each year tax officials harvested in season, fixed three price grades, and sold to the public.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，始命制國用使司印造懷孟等路司竹監竹引一萬道，每道取工墨一錢，凡發賣皆給引。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan the State Revenue Commission was first ordered to print ten thousand bamboo permits for the Bamboo Directorates of Huaimeng and other circuits; each permit charged one cash for production costs, and every sale required a permit.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 4 (1267) the State Revenue Commission first printed ten thousand bamboo permits for Huaimeng and other circuits at one cash each; every sale required one.

sentences.zh: 至二十二年，罷司竹監，聽民自賣輸稅。

translations.literal: By the twenty-second year the Bamboo Directorates were abolished, and the people were permitted to sell on their own while paying tax.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 22 (1285) the Bamboo Directorates were abolished and private sale with tax payment was permitted.

sentences.zh: 明年，又用郭畯言，於衛州復立竹課提舉司，凡輝、懷、嵩、洛、京襄、益都、宿、蘄等處竹貨皆隸焉。

translations.literal: The following year, again following Guo Jun's advice, a Bamboo Levy Intendant Office was re-established at Weizhou; all bamboo goods from Hui, Huai, Song, Luo, Jingxiang, Yidu, Su, Qi, and other places were placed under it.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on Guo Jun's advice, a Bamboo Levy Intendant Office was re-established at Weizhou over bamboo from Hui, Huai, Song, Luo, Jingxiang, Yidu, Su, Qi, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 在官者辦課，在民者輸稅。

translations.literal: Government groves furnished the levy; private holdings paid tax.
translations.idiomatic: Government groves paid the levy; private groves paid tax.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，又命陜西竹課提領司差官於輝、懷辦課。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year officials of the Shaanxi Bamboo Levy Commission were again ordered to be dispatched to Hui and Huai to handle the levy.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 23 (1286) the Shaanxi Bamboo Levy Commission again dispatched officers to Hui and Huai to collect the levy.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，丞相完澤言：「懷孟竹課，頻年斫伐已損。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Chancellor Wanze said: "The bamboo levy of Huaimeng — through years of repeated cutting it has already been depleted.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 29 (1292) Chancellor Wanze said: "The Huaimeng bamboo levy has been depleted by years of over-cutting.

sentences.zh: 課無所出，科民以輸。

translations.literal: The levy yields nothing, yet the people are assessed to pay.
translations.idiomatic: No levy can be raised, yet the people are still assessed to pay.

sentences.zh: 宜罷其課，長養數年。

translations.literal: It is fitting to abolish the levy and let the groves recover for several years."
translations.idiomatic: The levy should be suspended and the groves allowed to recover for several years."

sentences.zh: 」世祖從之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu assented.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu agreed.

sentences.zh: 此竹課之興革可考者也。

translations.literal: Such are the establishings and abolishings of the bamboo levy that can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Such are the recorded establishments and abolitions of the bamboo levy.

sentences.zh: 若夫硝、堿、木課，其興革無籍可考，故不著焉。

translations.literal: As for the saltpeter, alkali, and timber levies, their establishment and abolition have no records that can be verified; therefore they are not set down here.
translations.idiomatic: As for saltpeter, alkali, and timber levies, no records survive to verify their establishment or abolition, so they are not recorded here.

sentences.zh: 天歷元年歲課之數：金課：腹裏，四十錠四十七兩三錢。

translations.literal: The figures for the annual levies in the first year of Tianli: Gold levy: metropolitan region, forty ingots forty-seven taels three cash.
translations.idiomatic: Annual levy totals for Tianli 1 (1328): Gold levy — Metropolitan region: 40 ingots, 47 taels, 3 cash.

sentences.zh: 江浙省，一百八十錠一十五兩一錢。

translations.literal: Jiangzhe province, one hundred eighty ingots fifteen taels one cash.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhe: 180 ingots, 15 taels, 1 cash.

sentences.zh: 江西省，二錠四十兩五錢。

translations.literal: Jiangxi province, two ingots forty taels five cash.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi: 2 ingots, 40 taels, 5 cash.

sentences.zh: 湖廣省，八十錠二十兩一錢。

translations.literal: Huguang province, eighty ingots twenty taels one cash.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang: 80 ingots, 20 taels, 1 cash.

sentences.zh: 河南省，三十八兩六錢。

translations.literal: Henan province, thirty-eight taels six cash.
translations.idiomatic: Henan: 38 taels, 6 cash.

sentences.zh: 四川省，麩金七兩二錢。

translations.literal: Sichuan province, placer gold seven taels two cash.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan: 7 taels, 2 cash placer gold.

sentences.zh: 雲南省，一百八十四錠一兩九錢。

translations.literal: Yunnan province, one hundred eighty-four ingots one tael nine cash.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan: 184 ingots, 1 tael, 9 cash.

sentences.zh: 銀課：腹裏，一錠二十五兩。

translations.literal: Silver levy: metropolitan region, one ingot twenty-five taels.
translations.idiomatic: Silver levy — Metropolitan region: 1 ingot, 25 taels.

sentences.zh: 江浙省，一百一十五錠三十九兩二錢。

translations.literal: Jiangzhe province, one hundred fifteen ingots thirty-nine taels two cash.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhe: 115 ingots, 39 taels, 2 cash.

sentences.zh: 江西省，四百六十二錠三兩五錢。

translations.literal: Jiangxi province, four hundred sixty-two ingots three taels five cash.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi: 462 ingots, 3 taels, 5 cash.

sentences.zh: 湖廣省，二百三十六錠九兩。

translations.literal: Huguang province, two hundred thirty-six ingots nine taels.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang: 236 ingots, 9 taels.

sentences.zh: 雲南省，七百三十五錠三十四兩三錢。

translations.literal: Yunnan province, seven hundred thirty-five ingots thirty-four taels three cash.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan: 735 ingots, 34 taels, 3 cash.

sentences.zh: 銅課：

translations.literal: Copper levy:
translations.idiomatic: Copper levy:

sentences.zh: 雲南省二千三百八十斤。

translations.literal: Yunnan province, two thousand three hundred eighty jin.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan: 2,380 jin.

sentences.zh: 鐵課：

translations.literal: Iron levy:
translations.idiomatic: Iron levy:

sentences.zh: 江浙省，額外鐵二十四萬五千八百六十七斤，課鈔一千七百三錠一十四兩。

translations.literal: Jiangzhe province, additional-quota iron two hundred forty-five thousand eight hundred sixty-seven jin, levied notes one thousand seven hundred three ingots fourteen taels.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhe: additional-quota iron 245,867 jin; levy in Zhongtong notes 1,703 ingots, 14 taels.

sentences.zh: 江西省，二十一萬七千四百五十斤，課鈔一百七十六錠二十四兩。

translations.literal: Jiangxi province, two hundred seventeen thousand four hundred fifty jin, levied notes one hundred seventy-six ingots twenty-four taels.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi: 217,450 jin; levy in notes 176 ingots, 24 taels.

sentences.zh: 湖廣省，二十八萬二千五百九十五斤。

translations.literal: Huguang province, two hundred eighty-two thousand five hundred ninety-five jin.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang: 282,595 jin.

sentences.zh: 河南省，三千九百三十斤。

translations.literal: Henan province, three thousand nine hundred thirty jin.
translations.idiomatic: Henan: 3,930 jin.

sentences.zh: 陜西省，一萬斤。

translations.literal: Shaanxi province, ten thousand jin.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi: 10,000 jin.

sentences.zh: 雲南省，一十二萬四千七百一斤。

sentences.zh: ○鹽法

translations.literal: ○ Salt Monopoly Law
translations.idiomatic: Salt Monopoly Law

sentences.zh: 國之所資，其利最廣者莫如鹽。

translations.literal: Among what the state relies upon for revenue, none is broader in profit than salt.
translations.idiomatic: Of all the state's revenue sources, none yields profit on a wider scale than salt.

sentences.zh: 自漢桑弘羊始榷之，而後世未有遺其利者也。

translations.literal: Since Sang Hongyang of Han first monopolized it, later ages have never forgone its profit.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Sang Hongyang of the Han established the salt monopoly, no dynasty has willingly left its profits untapped.

sentences.zh: 元初，以酒醋、鹽稅、河泊、金、銀、鐵冶六色，取課於民，歲定白銀萬錠。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan, from the six categories of wine and vinegar, salt tax, river fisheries, gold, silver, and iron smelting, levies were taken from the people, fixed at ten thousand ingots of silver per year.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuan, six revenue streams—wine and vinegar, salt tax, river fisheries, gold, silver, and iron smelting—were taxed among the people, with an annual quota fixed at 10,000 ingots of silver.

sentences.zh: 太宗庚寅年，始行鹽法，每鹽一引重四百斤，其價銀一十兩。

translations.literal: In the gengyin year of Emperor Taizong, the salt law was first implemented; each salt permit weighed four hundred jin, its price ten taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's gengyin year (1230), the salt monopoly was introduced: each permit covered 400 jin of salt, priced at 10 taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統二年，減銀為七兩。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong under Emperor Shizu, the silver price was reduced to seven taels.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 2 (1261), the price was lowered to 7 taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年既取宋，而江南之鹽所入尤廣，每引改為中統鈔九貫。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan, after the Song had been taken, revenue from Jiangnan salt was especially broad; each permit was changed to nine strings of Zhongtong notes.
translations.idiomatic: After the conquest of the Song in Zhiyuan 13 (1276), revenue from Jiangnan salt grew especially large, and the price per permit was converted to 9 strings of Zhongtong notes.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，增為五十貫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, it was raised to fifty strings.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 26 (1289), it was raised to 50 strings.

sentences.zh: 元貞丙申，每引又增為六十五貫。

translations.literal: In bingshen of Yuanzhen, each permit was again raised to sixty-five strings.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanzhen bingshen (1296), each permit was raised again to 65 strings.

sentences.zh: 至大己酉至延祐乙卯，七年之間，累增為一百五十貫。

translations.literal: From jiyou of Zhidao to yimao of Yanyou, over seven years it was incrementally raised to one hundred fifty strings.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhidao jiyou (1309) to Yanyou yimao (1315), over seven years the price was raised step by step to 150 strings.

sentences.zh: 凡偽造鹽引者皆斬，籍其家產，付告人充賞。

translations.literal: All who counterfeit salt permits are decapitated; their household property is registered and confiscated, to be given to the informant as reward.
translations.idiomatic: Counterfeiting a salt permit carried the death penalty; the offender's entire estate was forfeited and given to the informant as a reward.

sentences.zh: 犯私鹽者徒二年，杖七十，止籍其財產之半；

translations.literal: Those who violate the private-salt ban are sentenced to two years' penal servitude and seventy blows with the staff, and only half their property is registered and confiscated;
translations.idiomatic: Smuggling private salt brought two years' penal servitude and seventy blows with the staff; only half the offender's property was confiscated;

sentences.zh: 有首告者，於所籍之內以其半賞之。

translations.literal: if there is an accuser, within what is confiscated half is given to him as reward.
translations.idiomatic: if someone reported the offense, half of what was confiscated was awarded to the informant.

sentences.zh: 行鹽各有郡邑，犯界者減私鹽罪一等，以其鹽之半沒官，半賞告者。

translations.literal: Each district has its allotted salt sales area; those who violate the boundary have the private-salt penalty reduced by one degree, half their salt confiscated by the government, and half given as reward to the informant.
translations.idiomatic: Each region had its designated sales territory; selling salt across the boundary reduced the penalty by one grade—half the salt was confiscated and half awarded to the informant.

sentences.zh: 然歲辦之課，難易各不同。

translations.literal: However, the annual quotas each differ in difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the difficulty of meeting the annual quotas varied widely from place to place.

sentences.zh: 有因自凝結而取者，解池之顆鹽也。

translations.literal: Some is obtained by natural crystallization—the crystal salt of Jiechi Pool.
translations.idiomatic: Some salt forms by natural crystallization—the crystal salt of Jiechi Pool.

sentences.zh: 有煮海而後成者，河間、山東、兩淮、兩浙、福建等處之末鹽也。

translations.literal: Some is produced by boiling the sea—the boiled sea salt of Hejian, Shandong, the Two Huai, the Two Zhe, Fujian, and other places.
translations.idiomatic: Other salt is made by boiling seawater—the boiled sea salt of Hejian, Shandong, the Two Huai, the Two Zhe, Fujian, and other regions.

sentences.zh: 惟四川之鹽出於井，深者數百尺，汲水煮之，視他處為最難。

translations.literal: Only Sichuan's salt comes from wells, some hundreds of feet deep; drawing the brine and boiling it is judged the most difficult of all places.
translations.idiomatic: Only Sichuan's salt came from brine wells, some hundreds of feet deep; drawing the brine and boiling it was the hardest production of all.

sentences.zh: 今各因其所產之地言之。

translations.literal: Now each is discussed according to the place where it is produced.
translations.idiomatic: What follows treats each producing region in turn.

sentences.zh: 大都之鹽：太宗丙申年，初於白陵港、三叉沽、大直沽等處置司，設熬煎辦，每引有工本錢。

translations.literal: Salt of Dadu: in the bingshen year of Taizong, offices were first established at Bailing Harbor, Sancha Estuary, Dazhi Estuary, and other places, with boiling operations set up; each permit had capital-cost funds.
translations.idiomatic: Salt in the Dadu region: In Taizong's bingshen year (1236), offices were first established at Bailing Harbor, Sancha Estuary, Dazhi Estuary, and elsewhere for boiling operations; each permit included a capital subsidy.

sentences.zh: 世祖至元二年，又增寶坻三鹽場，竈戶工本，每引為中統鈔三兩，與清、滄等。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan under Emperor Shizu, three salt fields at Baodi were added; capital for salt workers, each permit being three taels of Zhongtong notes, the same as Qingzhou, Cangzhou, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In Shizu's Zhiyuan 2 (1265), three salt fields at Baodi were added; the workers' capital subsidy was set at 3 taels of Zhongtong notes per permit—the same rate as at Qing and Cang.

sentences.zh: 八年，以大都民戶多食私鹽，因虧國課，驗口給以食鹽。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, because households in Dadu consumed much private salt and thus diminished state revenues, salt for consumption was allotted according to registered population.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, because Dadu households consumed so much private salt that state revenue suffered, salt rations were distributed according to registered population.

sentences.zh: 十九年，罷大都及河間、山東三鹽運司，設戶部尚書、員外郎各一員，別給印，令於大都置局賣引，鹽商買引，赴各場關鹽發賣。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, the three salt transport commissions of Dadu, Hejian, and Shandong were abolished; one Minister of Revenue and one Vice Minister were appointed, each given a separate seal, and ordered to establish an office in Dadu to sell permits; salt merchants bought permits and went to each field to collect salt for resale.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, the three salt transport commissions of Dadu, Hejian, and Shandong were abolished. One Minister of Revenue and one Vice Minister were appointed, each with a separate seal, to open an office in Dadu selling permits; merchants purchased permits and collected salt at the various fields for resale.

sentences.zh: 每歲竈戶工本，省臺遣官逐季分給之。

translations.literal: Each year the capital funds for salt workers were distributed by officials dispatched from the secretariat and censorate, quarterly.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the capital subsidy for salt workers was distributed quarterly by officials sent from the Secretariat and Censorate.

sentences.zh: 十九年，改立大都蘆臺越支三叉沽鹽使司一。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, one Salt Commissionerate for Dadu, Lutai, Yuezhi, and Sancha Estuary was established.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, one Salt Commissionerate was established for Dadu, Lutai, Yuezhi, and Sancha Estuary.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，復立三叉沽、蘆臺、越支三鹽使司。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, the three Salt Commissionerates of Sancha Estuary, Lutai, and Yuezhi were re-established.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, the three Salt Commissionerates of Sancha Estuary, Lutai, and Yuezhi were re-established.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，增竈戶工本，每引為中統鈔八兩。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, the capital for salt workers was increased; each permit was eight taels of Zhongtong notes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, the workers' capital subsidy was raised to 8 taels of Zhongtong notes per permit.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以歲饑減鹽課一萬引，入京兆鹽運司添辦。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, because of famine that year, the salt levy was reduced by ten thousand permits, the shortfall to be made up by the Jingzhao Salt Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, a famine year, the salt quota was cut by 10,000 permits, with the Jingzhao Salt Transport Commission assigned to make up the difference.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，遂罷大都鹽運司，並入河間。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade, the Dadu Salt Transport Commission was then abolished and merged into Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 1 (1297), the Dadu Salt Transport Commission was abolished and merged into Hejian.

sentences.zh: 河間之鹽：太宗庚寅年，始立河間稅課所，置鹽場，撥竈戶二千三百七十六隸之，每鹽一袋，重四百斤。

translations.literal: Salt of Hejian: in the gengyin year of Taizong, the Hejian Tax Office was first established and salt fields set up; two thousand three hundred seventy-six salt-worker households were assigned to it; each bag of salt weighed four hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: Salt in the Hejian region: In Taizong's gengyin year (1230), the Hejian Tax Office was established and salt fields opened; 2,376 salt-worker households were assigned. Each bag weighed 400 jin.

sentences.zh: 甲午年，立鹽運司。

translations.literal: In the jiawu year, a Salt Transport Commission was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiawu year (1234), a Salt Transport Commission was established.

sentences.zh: 庚子年，改立提舉鹽榷所，歲辦三萬四千七百袋。

translations.literal: In the gengzi year, it was changed to a Salt Monopoly Intendant Office, with an annual quota of thirty-four thousand seven hundred bags.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengzi year (1240), it was reorganized as a Salt Monopoly Intendant Office with an annual quota of 34,700 bags.

sentences.zh: 癸卯年，改立提舉滄清鹽課使所，歲辦鹽九萬袋。

translations.literal: In the guimao year, it was changed to the Cang-Qing Salt Levy Commissionerate, with an annual salt quota of ninety thousand bags.
translations.idiomatic: In the guimao year (1243), it became the Cang-Qing Salt Levy Commissionerate, with an annual quota of 90,000 bags.

sentences.zh: 定宗四年，改真定河間等路課程所為提舉鹽榷滄清鹽使所。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Emperor Dingzong, the Revenue Office of Zhending, Hejian, and other circuits was changed to the Cang-Qing Salt Monopoly Commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: In Dingzong's fourth year (1249), the Zhending-Hejian Revenue Office was reorganized as the Cang-Qing Salt Monopoly Commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 憲宗二年，又改河間課程所為提舉滄清深鹽使所。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Xianzong, the Hejian Revenue Office was again changed to the Cang-Qing-Shen Salt Commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianzong 2 (1252), the Hejian Revenue Office was again reorganized as the Cang-Qing-Shen Salt Commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 八年，每袋增鹽至四百五十斤。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, each bag was increased to four hundred fifty jin of salt.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the weight per bag was raised to 450 jin.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統元年，改立宣撫司提領滄清深鹽使所。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong under Emperor Shizu, it was changed to a Pacification Commission supervising the Cang-Qing-Shen Salt Commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: In Shizu's Zhongtong 1 (1260), a Pacification Commission was placed over the Cang-Qing-Shen Salt Commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 四年，改滄清深鹽提領所為轉運司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Cang-Qing-Shen Salt Intendant Office was changed to a Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, the Cang-Qing-Shen Salt Intendant Office became a Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 是年，辦銀七千六十五錠，米三萬三千三百餘石。

translations.literal: That year, it furnished seven thousand sixty-five ingots of silver and more than thirty-three thousand three hundred shi of rice.
translations.idiomatic: That year, it delivered 7,065 ingots of silver and more than 33,300 shi of rice.

sentences.zh: 至元元年，又增三之一焉。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhiyuan, it was again increased by one third.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 1 (1264), the quota was raised by one third.

sentences.zh: 二年，改立河間都轉運司，歲辦九萬五千袋。

translations.literal: In the second year, the Hejian Metropolitan Transport Commission was established, with an annual quota of ninety-five thousand bags.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, the Hejian Metropolitan Transport Commission was established, with an annual quota of 95,000 bags.

sentences.zh: 七年，始定例歲煎鹽十萬引，辦課銀一萬錠。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, regulations were first fixed for one hundred thousand permits of salt boiled annually, with a levy of ten thousand ingots of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, regulations fixed annual production at 100,000 permits of boiled salt, with a levy of 10,000 ingots of silver.

sentences.zh: 十二年，改立都轉運使司，添竈戶九百餘，增鹽課二十萬引。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the Metropolitan Transport Commissionerate was established; more than nine hundred salt-worker households were added, and the salt levy increased by two hundred thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the Metropolitan Transport Commissionerate was established; over 900 salt-worker households were added, and the salt levy rose by 200,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以河間竈戶勞苦，增工本為中統鈔三貫。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, because the Hejian salt workers suffered hardship, the capital subsidy was increased to three strings of Zhongtong notes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, because Hejian salt workers labored under great hardship, the capital subsidy was raised to 3 strings of Zhongtong notes.

sentences.zh: 是年，又增竈戶七百八十六。

translations.literal: That year, seven hundred eighty-six salt-worker households were also added.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, 786 salt-worker households were added.

sentences.zh: 十九年，罷河間都轉運司，改立清、滄鹽使司二。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, the Hejian Metropolitan Transport Commission was abolished and two Salt Commissionerates, Qing and Cang, were established.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, the Hejian Metropolitan Transport Commission was abolished and replaced by two Salt Commissionerates, at Qing and Cang.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，復立河間等路都轉運鹽使司，增鹽課為二十九萬六百引。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, the Hejian Circuit Metropolitan Transport Salt Commissionerate was re-established; the salt levy was increased to two hundred ninety thousand six hundred permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, the Hejian Circuit Metropolitan Transport Salt Commissionerate was re-established, with the salt levy raised to 290,600 permits.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，改立河間都轉運司，通辦鹽酒稅課。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the Hejian Metropolitan Transport Commission was established, handling salt, wine, and tax levies together.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, the Hejian Metropolitan Transport Commission was established to handle salt, wine, and tax levies together.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，增工本為中統鈔五貫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, the capital subsidy was increased to five strings of Zhongtong notes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, the capital subsidy was raised to 5 strings of Zhongtong notes.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，增竈戶四百七十，辦鹽三十五萬引。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year, four hundred seventy salt-worker households were added; salt production was three hundred fifty thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year, 470 salt-worker households were added, with production at 350,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，又增至四十五萬引。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, it was again increased to four hundred fifty thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 1 (1308), production was raised again to 450,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，以虧課，停煎五萬引。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou, because of revenue shortfall, boiling was halted for fifty thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 1 (1314), because of revenue shortfall, production was cut by 50,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 自是至天歷，皆歲辦四十萬引，所隸之場，凡二十有二。

translations.literal: From then until Tianli, the annual quota was always four hundred thousand permits; the fields subordinate to it numbered twenty-two in all.
translations.idiomatic: From then until Tianli, the annual quota stood at 400,000 permits, across twenty-two subordinate salt fields.

sentences.zh: 山東之鹽：太宗庚寅年，始立益都課稅所，撥竈戶二千一百七十隸之，每銀一兩，得鹽四十斤。

translations.literal: Salt of Shandong: in the gengyin year of Taizong, the Yidu Tax Office was first established; two thousand one hundred seventy salt-worker households were assigned to it; for each tael of silver, forty jin of salt was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Salt in the Shandong region: In Taizong's gengyin year (1230), the Yidu Tax Office was established with 2,170 salt-worker households assigned. Each tael of silver yielded 40 jin of salt.

sentences.zh: 甲午年，立山東鹽運司。

translations.literal: In the jiawu year, the Shandong Salt Transport Commission was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiawu year (1234), the Shandong Salt Transport Commission was established.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，歲辦銀二千五百錠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, the annual quota was two thousand five hundred ingots of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongtong 1 (1260), the annual levy was 2,500 ingots of silver.

sentences.zh: 三年，命課稅隸山東都轉運司。

translations.literal: In the third year, it was ordered that tax levies be placed under the Shandong Metropolitan Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, levies were placed under the Shandong Metropolitan Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 四年，令益都山東民戶，月買食鹽三斤；

translations.literal: In the fourth year, it was ordered that households in Yidu and Shandong purchase three jin of table salt per month;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, households in Yidu and Shandong were required to purchase 3 jin of table salt per month;

sentences.zh: 竈戶逃亡者，招民戶補之。

translations.literal: when salt workers fled, common households were recruited to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: when salt workers fled, ordinary households were recruited to fill their places.

sentences.zh: 是歲，辦銀三千三百錠。

translations.literal: That year, it furnished three thousand three hundred ingots of silver.
translations.idiomatic: That year, the levy came to 3,300 ingots of silver.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，改立山東轉運司，辦課銀四千六百錠一十九兩。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan, the Shandong Transport Commission was established; the levy was four thousand six hundred ingots nineteen taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 2 (1265), the Shandong Transport Commission was established, with a levy of 4,600 ingots and 19 taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 是年，戶部造山東鹽引。

translations.literal: That year, the Ministry of Revenue produced Shandong salt permits.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, the Ministry of Revenue issued Shandong salt permits.

sentences.zh: 六年，增歲辦鹽為七萬一千九百九十八引，自是每歲增之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the annual salt quota was increased to seventy-one thousand nine hundred ninety-eight permits; from then on it increased each year.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, the annual salt quota was raised to 71,998 permits; thereafter it rose every year.

sentences.zh: 至十二年，改立山東都轉運司，歲辦鹽一十四萬七千四百八十七引。

translations.literal: By the twelfth year, the Shandong Metropolitan Transport Commission was established; the annual salt quota was one hundred forty-seven thousand four hundred eighty-seven permits.
translations.idiomatic: By the twelfth year, the Shandong Metropolitan Transport Commission was established, with an annual quota of 147,487 permits.

sentences.zh: 十八年，增竈戶七百，又增鹽為一十六萬五千四百八十七引，竈戶工本錢亦增為中統鈔三貫。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, seven hundred salt pan households were added, and salt was again increased by one hundred sixty-five thousand four hundred eighty-seven permits; the capital subsidy for salt pan households was also increased to three strings of Zhongtong notes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, 700 salt pan households were added and production increased by 165,487 permits; the capital subsidy for salt pan households was raised to 3 strings of Zhongtong notes.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，歲辦鹽二十七萬一千七百四十二引。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the annual salt quota was two hundred seventy-one thousand seven hundred forty-two permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, the annual quota came to 271,742 permits.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，減為二十二萬引。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, it was reduced to two hundred twenty thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, the quota was cut to 220,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 大德十年，又增為二十五萬引。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dade, it was again increased to two hundred fifty thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 10 (1306), the quota was raised again to 250,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 至大元年之後，歲辦正、余鹽為三十一萬引，所隸之場，凡一十有九。

translations.literal: After the first year of Zhidao, the annual regular and surplus salt quota was three hundred ten thousand permits; the subordinate salt fields numbered nineteen in all.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhidao 1 (1308), the annual regular and surplus salt quota stood at 310,000 permits, across nineteen subordinate salt fields.

sentences.zh: 河東之鹽：出解州鹽池，池方一百二十里，每歲五月，場官伺池鹽生結，令夫搬摝鹽花。

translations.literal: Salt of Hedong: it came from the salt ponds of Xiezhou; the ponds measured one hundred twenty li square; each year in the fifth month, field officials watched for pond salt to crystallize and ordered laborers to gather and rake the salt blossoms.
translations.idiomatic: Salt in the Hedong region came from the salt ponds at Xiezhou, covering an area of 120 li square. Every year in the fifth month, field officials watched for salt to crystallize in the ponds and ordered laborers to gather and rake the salt blossoms.

sentences.zh: 其法必值亢陽，池鹽方就，或遇陰雨，則不能成矣。

translations.literal: By this method it had to coincide with prolonged drought before pond salt could form; if rain came, it could not be produced.
translations.idiomatic: This method required prolonged drought for the pond salt to form; if rain came, production failed.

sentences.zh: 太宗庚寅年，始立平陽府征收課稅所，從實辦課，每鹽四十斤，得銀一兩。

translations.literal: In Taizong's gengyin year, the Pingyang Prefecture Tax Collection Office was first established; levies were collected according to actual yield—forty jin of salt yielded one tael of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's gengyin year (1230), the Pingyang Prefecture Tax Collection Office was established, with levies collected on actual yield: 40 jin of salt per tael of silver.

sentences.zh: 癸巳年，撥新降戶一千，命鹽使姚行簡等修理鹽池損壞處所。

translations.literal: In the guisi year, one thousand newly submitted households were assigned, and Salt Commissioner Yao Xingjian and others were ordered to repair damaged sections of the salt ponds.
translations.idiomatic: In the guisi year (1233), 1,000 newly submitted households were assigned, and Salt Commissioner Yao Xingjian and others were ordered to repair damaged sections of the salt ponds.

sentences.zh: 憲宗壬子年，又增撥一千八十五戶，歲撈鹽一萬五千引，辦課銀三千錠。

translations.literal: In Xianzong's renzi year, another one thousand eighty-five households were added; annual dredged salt was fifteen thousand permits, with a levy of three thousand ingots of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianzong's renzi year (1252), another 1,085 households were assigned; annual dredged salt came to 15,000 permits, with a levy of 3,000 ingots of silver.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統二年，初立陜西轉運司，仍置解鹽司於路村。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong under Emperor Shizu, the Shaanxi Transport Commission was first established, and the Xie Salt Office remained placed at Lucun.
translations.idiomatic: In Shizu's Zhongtong 2 (1261), the Shaanxi Transport Commission was established, with the Xie Salt Office kept at Lucun.

sentences.zh: 三年，以太原民戶自煎小鹽，歲辦課銀一百五十錠。

translations.literal: In the third year, because Taiyuan common households boiled small salt on their own, the annual levy was one hundred fifty ingots of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, because Taiyuan households boiled small salt on their own, the annual levy came to 150 ingots of silver.

sentences.zh: 五年，又增小鹽課銀為二百五十錠。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the small-salt levy in silver was again increased to two hundred fifty ingots.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, the small-salt levy was raised to 250 ingots of silver.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，諭陜西四川，以所辦鹽課赴行制國用使司輸納，鹽引令制國用使司給降。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan, Shaanxi and Sichuan were instructed that salt levies collected were to be delivered to the Commissariat for State Revenue, and salt permits were to be issued by the Commissariat for State Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 3 (1266), Shaanxi and Sichuan were instructed to deliver collected salt levies to the Commissariat for State Revenue, with salt permits to be issued by that office.

sentences.zh: 四年，立陜西四川轉運司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Shaanxi-Sichuan Transport Commission was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, the Shaanxi-Sichuan Transport Commission was established.

sentences.zh: 六年，立太原提舉鹽使司，直隸制國用使司。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Taiyuan Salt Commissionerate was established, directly under the Commissariat for State Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, the Taiyuan Salt Commissionerate was established, reporting directly to the Commissariat for State Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十年，命撈鹽戶九百八十餘，每丁撈鹽一石，給工價鈔五錢。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, more than nine hundred eighty salt-dredging households were assigned; each adult male dredged one shi of salt, and wages of five qian in notes were paid.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, over 980 salt-dredging households were assigned; each adult male dredged one shi of salt and was paid wages of 5 qian in notes.

sentences.zh: 歲辦鹽六萬四千引，計中統鈔一萬一千五百二十錠。

translations.literal: The annual salt quota was sixty-four thousand permits, totaling eleven thousand five hundred twenty ingots of Zhongtong notes.
translations.idiomatic: The annual quota stood at 64,000 permits, totaling 11,520 ingots of Zhongtong notes.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，改立陜西都轉運司，兼辦鹽、酒、醋、竹等課。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the Shaanxi Metropolitan Transport Commission was established, also handling levies on salt, wine, vinegar, bamboo, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, the Shaanxi Metropolitan Transport Commission was reorganized to handle levies on salt, wine, vinegar, bamboo, and related goods.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，減大都鹽課一萬引，入京兆鹽司添辦。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, ten thousand permits were cut from the Dadu salt levy and added to the Jingzhao Salt Commission's quota.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, 10,000 permits were transferred from the Dadu salt levy to the Jingzhao Salt Commission.

sentences.zh: 是年五月，又革京兆鹽司一，止存鹽運司。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year, one Jingzhao Salt Commission was abolished, leaving only the Salt Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In May of that year, one Jingzhao Salt Commission was abolished, leaving only the Salt Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 大德十一年，增歲額為八萬二千引。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade, the annual quota was increased to eighty-two thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 11 (1307), the annual quota was raised to 82,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，又增煎余鹽為二萬引，通為一十萬二千引。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, surplus boiled salt was again increased by twenty thousand permits, bringing the total to one hundred two thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 1 (1308), surplus boiled salt was increased by 20,000 permits, for a combined total of 102,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 延祐三年，以池為雨所壞，止辦課鈔八萬二千餘錠。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yanyou, because the ponds were damaged by rain, only eighty-two thousand-odd ingots in note levies were collected.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 3 (1316), rain damage to the ponds limited collections to just over 82,000 ingots in note levies.

sentences.zh: 於是晉寧、陜西之民改食常仁紅鹽，懷孟、河南之民改食滄鹽。

translations.literal: Thereupon the people of Jinning and Shaanxi switched to eating Changren red salt, and the people of Huaiqing and Henan switched to eating Cang salt.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the people of Jinning and Shaanxi began eating Changren red salt, while those of Huaiqing and Henan turned to Cang salt.

sentences.zh: 五年，乃免河南、懷孟、南陽三路今歲陜西鹽課，仍授鹽運使暨所臨路府州縣正官兼知渠堰事，責以疏通壅塞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the Shaanxi salt levies for Henan, Huaiqing, and Nanyang circuits were remitted for that year; the Salt Transport Commissioner and the chief officials of the circuits, prefectures, and counties under his jurisdiction were concurrently charged with canal and dyke affairs and held responsible for clearing blockages.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Shaanxi salt levies for Henan, Huaiqing, and Nanyang were remitted for that year; the Salt Transport Commissioner and circuit, prefecture, and county officials under his jurisdiction were also charged with canal and dyke maintenance and held responsible for clearing blockages.

sentences.zh: 六年，改陜西運司為河東解鹽等處都轉運鹽使司，直隸中書省。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Shaanxi Transport Commission was reorganized as the Hedong Xie Salt Metropolitan Salt Transport Commissionerate, directly under the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, the Shaanxi Transport Commission became the Hedong Xie Salt Metropolitan Salt Transport Commissionerate, reporting directly to the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十月，罷陜西行省所委巡鹽官六十八員，添設通判一員，別鑄分司印二。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, sixty-eight salt-inspection officials delegated by the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat were abolished; one assistant prefect was added, and two separate branch-office seals were cast.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, 68 salt-inspection officials delegated by the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat were abolished; one assistant prefect was added, and two branch-office seals were cast.

sentences.zh: 又罷撈鹽提領二十員，改立提領所二，增余鹽五百料。

translations.literal: Twenty salt-dredging intendant posts were also abolished and replaced with two intendant offices; surplus salt was increased by five hundred liao.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty salt-dredging intendant posts were abolished and replaced with two intendant offices; the surplus salt quota was increased by 500 liao.

sentences.zh: 是年，實撈鹽一十八萬四千五百引。

translations.literal: That year, salt actually dredged came to one hundred eighty-four thousand five hundred permits.
translations.idiomatic: That year, actual dredged salt production came to 184,500 permits.

sentences.zh: 天歷二年，辦課鈔三十九萬五千三百九十五錠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianli, note levies amounted to three hundred ninety-five thousand three hundred ninety-five ingots.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 2 (1329), note levies came to 395,395 ingots.

sentences.zh: 四川之鹽：為場凡一十有二，為井凡九十有五，在成都、夔府、重慶、敘南、嘉定、順慶、潼川、紹慶等路萬山之間。

translations.literal: Salt of Sichuan: there were twelve salt fields and ninety-five salt wells, scattered among the myriad mountains in the circuits of Chengdu, Kuizhou, Chongqing, Xunan, Jiading, Shunqing, Tongchuan, Shaoqing, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Salt in Sichuan comprised twelve salt fields and ninety-five salt wells, scattered among the mountains of Chengdu, Kuizhou, Chongqing, Xunan, Jiading, Shunqing, Tongchuan, Shaoqing, and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 元初，設拘搉課稅所，分撥竈戶五千九百餘隸之，從實辦課。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan, a Monopoly Tax Office was established; more than five thousand nine hundred salt pan households were assigned to it, with levies collected according to actual yield.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yuan founding, a Monopoly Tax Office was established with over 5,900 salt pan households assigned, and levies collected on actual yield.

sentences.zh: 後為鹽井廢壞，四川軍民多食解鹽。

translations.literal: Later, because the salt wells fell into ruin, soldiers and civilians in Sichuan mostly ate Xie salt.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as salt wells fell into disrepair, soldiers and civilians in Sichuan relied heavily on Xie salt from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，立興元四川鹽運司，修理鹽井，仍禁解鹽不許過界。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan, the Xingyuan-Sichuan Salt Transport Commission was established to repair the salt wells, and Xie salt was still forbidden to cross the border.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 2 (1265), the Xingyuan-Sichuan Salt Transport Commission was established to repair salt wells, while Xie salt remained barred from crossing into the province.

sentences.zh: 八年，罷四川茶鹽運司。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the Sichuan Tea and Salt Transport Commission was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the Sichuan Tea and Salt Transport Commission was abolished.

sentences.zh: 十六年，復立之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, it was reestablished.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, it was reestablished.

sentences.zh: 十八年，並鹽課入四川道宣慰司。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, salt levies were merged into the Sichuan Circuit Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, salt levies were placed under the Sichuan Circuit Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 十九年，復立陜西四川轉運司，通辦鹽課。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, the Shaanxi-Sichuan Transport Commission was reestablished to handle salt levies comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, the Shaanxi-Sichuan Transport Commission was reestablished to handle salt levies jointly.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，改立四川鹽茶運司，分京兆運司為二，歲煎鹽一萬四百五十一引。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, the Sichuan Salt and Tea Transport Commission was established; the Jingzhao Transport Commission was split in two; annual boiled salt was ten thousand four hundred fifty-one permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, the Sichuan Salt and Tea Transport Commission was established and the Jingzhao Transport Commission was divided; annual boiled salt came to 10,451 permits.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，一萬七千一百五十二引。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, seventeen thousand one hundred fifty-two permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, production stood at 17,152 permits.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，以竈戶艱辛，減煎余鹽五千引。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing, because salt pan households suffered hardship, surplus boiled salt was reduced by five thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangqing 1 (1312), because salt pan households labored under great hardship, surplus boiled salt was cut by 5,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 天歷二年，辦鹽二萬八千九百一十引，計鈔八萬六千七百三十錠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianli, salt production was twenty-eight thousand nine hundred ten permits, totaling eighty-six thousand seven hundred thirty ingots of notes.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 2 (1329), production came to 28,910 permits, totaling 86,730 ingots of notes.

sentences.zh: 遼陽之鹽：太宗丁酉年，始命北京路征收課稅所，以大鹽泊硬鹽立隨車隨引載鹽之法，每鹽一石，價銀七錢半，帶納匠人米五升。

translations.literal: Salt of Liaoyang: in Taizong's dingyou year, the Beijing Circuit Tax Collection Office was first ordered to establish a method of loading salt with each cart and permit using hard salt from Dayanbo; each shi of salt cost seven qian and a half in silver, with five sheng of artisan rice payable additionally.
translations.idiomatic: Salt in Liaoyang: In Taizong's dingyou year (1237), the Beijing Circuit Tax Collection Office established a system of cart-and-permit salt transport using hard salt from Dayanbo; each shi of salt cost 7.5 qian of silver, plus 5 sheng of artisan rice.

sentences.zh: 癸卯年，合懶路歲辦課白布二千匹，恤品路布一千匹。

translations.literal: In the guimao year, Helan Circuit furnished an annual levy of two thousand bolts of white cloth, and Xipin Circuit one thousand bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: In the guimao year (1243), Helan Circuit paid an annual levy of 2,000 bolts of white cloth, and Xipin Circuit 1,000 bolts.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，立開元等路運司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan, the Kaiyuan Circuit Transport Commission was established.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 4 (1267), the Kaiyuan Circuit Transport Commission was established.

sentences.zh: 五年，禁東京懿州乞石兒硬鹽，不許過塗河界。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, hard salt from Tokyo, Yizhou, and Qishier was banned from crossing the Tuh River border.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, hard salt from Tokyo, Yizhou, and Qishier was barred from crossing the Tuh River border.

sentences.zh: 是年，諭各位下鹽課如例輸納。

translations.literal: That year, it was proclaimed that salt levies from princely establishments and other ranks were to be paid according to regulation.
