translations.idiomatic: That year, it was ordered that salt levies from princely establishments and other ranks be paid according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，灤州四處鹽課，舊納羊一千者，亦令如例輸鈔。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, salt levies from four places in Luanzhou that had formerly been paid in sheep at one thousand each were also required to be paid in notes according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, four Luanzhou salt stations that had paid levies in sheep—1,000 per station—were required to pay in notes instead.

sentences.zh: 延祐二年，又命食鹽人戶，歲辦課鈔，每兩率加五焉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanyou, households that consumed salt were again ordered to furnish annual note levies, with an additional five added for every two taels at the standard rate.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 2 (1315), salt-consuming households were again required to pay annual note levies, with an additional 5 added for every 2 taels at the standard rate.

sentences.zh: 兩淮之鹽：至元十三年命提舉馬裏範張依宋舊例辦課，每引重三百斤，其價為中統鈔八兩。

translations.literal: Salt of the Two Huai: in the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan it was ordered that Intendant Malifan Zhang handle levies according to Song precedent; each permit weighed three hundred jin, its price being eight taels of Zhongtong notes.
translations.idiomatic: Salt in the Two Huai region: In Zhiyuan 13 (1276), Intendant Malifan Zhang was ordered to collect levies under Song precedent, with each permit weighing 300 jin at a price of 8 taels of Zhongtong notes.

sentences.zh: 十四年，立兩淮都轉運使司，每引始改為四百斤。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the Two Huai Metropolitan Transport Commissionerate was established; each permit was first changed to four hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, the Two Huai Metropolitan Transport Commissionerate was established, and the standard permit weight was set at 400 jin.

sentences.zh: 十六年，額辦五十八萬七千六百二十三引。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the quota was five hundred eighty-seven thousand six hundred twenty-three permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, the quota stood at 587,623 permits.

sentences.zh: 十八年，增為八十萬引。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, it was increased to eight hundred thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, the quota was raised to 800,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，減一十五萬引。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, one hundred fifty thousand permits were cut.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, the quota was cut by 150,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 三十年，以襄陽民改食揚州鹽，又增八千二百引。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, because the people of Xiangyang switched to eating Yangzhou salt, the quota was again increased by eight thousand two hundred permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, because Xiangyang residents began eating Yangzhou salt, the quota was increased by another 8,200 permits.

sentences.zh: 大德四年，諭兩淮鹽運司設關防之法，凡鹽商經批驗所發賣者，所官收批引牙錢，其不經批驗所者，本倉就收之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dade, the Two Huai Salt Transport Commission was instructed to establish checkpoint regulations: when salt merchants sold salt that had passed through inspection stations, the station officials collected seal-and-permit broker fees; when they had not passed through inspection stations, the original warehouse collected them.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 4 (1300), the Two Huai Salt Transport Commission established checkpoint regulations: when merchants sold salt through inspection stations, station officials collected permit-seal fees; otherwise the issuing warehouse collected them.

sentences.zh: 八年，以竈戶艱辛，遣官究議，停煎五萬餘引。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, because salt pan households suffered hardship, officials were dispatched to investigate, and boiling was halted for more than fifty thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, because salt pan households labored under great hardship, officials were dispatched to investigate, and production was cut by over 50,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 天歷二年，額辦正余鹽九十五萬七十五引，計中統鈔二百八十五萬二百二十五錠，所隸之場凡二十有九，其工本鈔亦自四兩遞增至十兩云。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianli, the regular and surplus salt quota was nine hundred fifty thousand seventy-five permits, totaling two million eight hundred fifty thousand two hundred twenty-five ingots of Zhongtong notes; subordinate salt fields numbered twenty-nine in all; capital subsidies in notes also rose in stages from four taels to ten taels, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 2 (1329), the regular and surplus salt quota stood at 950,075 permits, totaling 2,850,225 ingots of Zhongtong notes across twenty-nine subordinate fields; capital subsidies in notes rose in stages from 4 to 10 taels.

sentences.zh: 兩浙之鹽：至元十四年，立運司，歲辦九萬二千一百四十八引。

translations.literal: Salt of the Two Zhe: in the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan the Transport Commission was established; the annual quota was ninety-two thousand one hundred forty-eight permits.
translations.idiomatic: Salt in the Two Zhe region: In Zhiyuan 14 (1277), a Transport Commission was established with an annual quota of 92,148 permits.

sentences.zh: 每引分作二袋，每袋依宋十八界會子，折中統鈔九兩。

translations.literal: Each permit was divided into two bags; each bag, according to the Song Eighteenth-Realm huizi, was converted to nine taels of Zhongtong notes.
translations.idiomatic: Each permit was divided into two bags; each bag was priced at 9 taels of Zhongtong notes, converted from the Song Eighteenth-Realm huizi rate.

sentences.zh: 十八年，增至二十一萬八千五百六十二引。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, it was increased to two hundred eighteen thousand five hundred sixty-two permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, the quota rose to 218,562 permits.

sentences.zh: 十九年，每引於舊價之上增鈔四貫。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, each permit had four strings of notes added above the old price.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, each permit's price was raised by 4 strings of notes above the previous rate.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，置常平局，以平民間鹽價。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, a Constant-Equilibrium Bureau was established to stabilize market salt prices.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, a Constant-Equilibrium Bureau was established to stabilize private-market salt prices.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，增歲辦為四十五萬引。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the annual quota was increased to four hundred fifty thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, the annual quota was raised to 450,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，減十萬引。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, one hundred thousand permits were cut.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, the quota was cut by 100,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 三十年，置局賣鹽魚鹽於海濱漁所。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, bureaus were established to sell salted fish salt at coastal fishing stations.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, sales bureaus for fish salt were established at coastal fishing stations.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，並煎鹽地四十四所為三十四場。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, forty-four salt-boiling sites were consolidated into thirty-four fields.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, forty-four salt-boiling sites were consolidated into thirty-four salt fields.

sentences.zh: 大德三年，立兩浙鹽運司檢校所四。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dade, four inspectorate offices of the Two Zhe Salt Transport Commission were established.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 3 (1299), four inspectorate offices were established under the Two Zhe Salt Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 五年，增額為四十萬引。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the quota was increased to four hundred thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, the quota was raised to 400,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，又增余鹽五萬引。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, surplus salt was again increased by fifty thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 1 (1308), surplus salt was increased by another 50,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 延祐六年，罷四檢校所，立嘉興、紹興等處鹽倉官，三十四場各場鹽運官一員，歲辦五十萬引。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yanyou, the four inspectorate offices were abolished; salt warehouse officials were established at Jiaxing, Shaoxing, and other places; each of the thirty-four fields received one salt transport official; the annual quota was five hundred thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 6 (1319), the four inspectorates were abolished; salt warehouse officials were appointed at Jiaxing, Shaoxing, and elsewhere, with one transport official per field across thirty-four fields; the annual quota stood at 500,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 七年，各運司鹽課以十分為率，收白銀一分，每銀一錠，準鹽課四十錠。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, salt levies at each transport commission were reckoned by tens; one tenth was collected in white silver; each ingot of silver was equivalent to forty ingots of salt levy.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, at each transport commission one tenth of salt levies was collected in silver, with each ingot of silver equivalent to 40 ingots of salt levy.

sentences.zh: 其工本鈔，浙西一十一場正鹽每引遞增至二十兩，余鹽至二十五兩；

translations.literal: As for capital subsidies in notes, at the eleven fields of Western Zhe, regular salt per permit rose in stages to twenty taels, and surplus salt to twenty-five taels;
translations.idiomatic: For capital subsidies in notes, at the eleven Western Zhe fields, regular salt subsidies per permit rose in stages to 20 taels and surplus salt to 25 taels;

sentences.zh: 浙東二十三場正鹽每引遞增至二十五兩，余鹽至三十兩云。

translations.literal: at the twenty-three fields of Eastern Zhe, regular salt per permit rose in stages to twenty-five taels, and surplus salt to thirty taels, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: at the twenty-three Eastern Zhe fields, regular salt subsidies per permit rose in stages to 25 taels and surplus salt to 30 taels.

sentences.zh: 福建之鹽：至元十三年，始收其課，為鹽六千五十五引。

translations.literal: Salt of Fujian: in the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan levies were first collected; salt production was six thousand fifty-five permits.
translations.idiomatic: Salt in Fujian: In Zhiyuan 13 (1276), levies were first collected, with production at 6,055 permits.

sentences.zh: 十四年，立市舶司，兼辦鹽課。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the Maritime Trade Commissionerate was established, also handling salt levies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, the Maritime Trade Commissionerate was established, also handling salt levies.

sentences.zh: 二十年，增至五萬四千二百引。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, it was increased to fifty-four thousand two hundred permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, production rose to 54,200 permits.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，改立福建等處轉運鹽使司，歲辦鹽六萬引。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, the Fujian Metropolitan Salt Transport Commissionerate was established; the annual salt quota was sixty thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, the Fujian Metropolitan Salt Transport Commissionerate was established with an annual quota of 60,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，罷福建鹽運司及鹽使司，改立福建鹽課提舉司，增鹽為七萬引。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, the Fujian Salt Transport Commission and Salt Commissionerate were abolished and replaced by the Fujian Salt Levy Commissionerate; salt production was increased to seventy thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, the Fujian Salt Transport Commission and Salt Commissionerate were abolished and replaced by the Fujian Salt Levy Commissionerate; production was raised to 70,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 大德四年，復立鹽運司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dade, the Salt Transport Commission was reestablished.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 4 (1300), the Salt Transport Commission was reestablished.

sentences.zh: 九年，又罷之，並入本道宣慰司。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, it was again abolished and merged into the circuit Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, it was abolished again and placed under the circuit Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 十年，又立鹽課都提舉司，增鹽至十萬引。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Salt Levy Metropolitan Commissionerate was again established; salt production was increased to one hundred thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, the Salt Levy Metropolitan Commissionerate was reestablished and production raised to 100,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，又增至十三萬引。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, it was again increased to one hundred thirty thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 1 (1308), production was raised again to 130,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 四年，改立福建鹽運司。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Fujian Salt Transport Commission was established.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, the Fujian Salt Transport Commission was reorganized.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，實辦課三十八萬七千七百八十三錠。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun, levies actually collected amounted to three hundred eighty-seven thousand seven hundred eighty-three ingots.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhishun 1 (1330), actual levies came to 387,783 ingots.

sentences.zh: 其工本鈔，煎鹽每引遞增至二十貫，曬鹽每引至一十七貫四錢。

translations.literal: Capital subsidies in notes for boiled salt per permit rose in stages to twenty strings; for sun-dried salt per permit to seventeen strings four qian.
translations.idiomatic: Capital subsidies in notes rose in stages to 20 strings per permit for boiled salt and 17 strings 4 qian for sun-dried salt.

sentences.zh: 所隸之場有七。

translations.literal: The subordinate salt fields numbered seven.
translations.idiomatic: There were seven subordinate salt fields.

sentences.zh: 廣東之鹽：至元十三年，克廣州，因宋之舊，立提舉司，從實辦課。

translations.literal: Salt of Guangdong: in the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan Guangzhou was taken; following Song practice, a Commissionerate was established, with levies collected according to actual yield.
translations.idiomatic: Salt in Guangdong: In Zhiyuan 13 (1276), after Guangzhou was taken, a Commissionerate was established under Song precedent, with levies collected on actual yield.

sentences.zh: 十六年，立江西鹽鐵茶都轉運司，所轄鹽使司六，各場立管勾。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the Jiangxi Salt, Iron, and Tea Metropolitan Transport Commission was established, with six salt commissionerates under its jurisdiction; each field had an overseer appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, the Jiangxi Salt, Iron, and Tea Metropolitan Transport Commission was established, supervising six salt commissionerates with an overseer appointed at each field.

sentences.zh: 是年，辦鹽六百二十一引。

translations.literal: That year, salt production was six hundred twenty-one permits.
translations.idiomatic: That year, production came to 621 permits.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，分江西鹽隸廣東宣慰司，歲辦一萬八百二十五引。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Jiangxi salt was placed under the Guangdong Pacification Commission; the annual quota was ten thousand eight hundred twenty-five permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, Jiangxi salt was placed under the Guangdong Pacification Commission, with an annual quota of 10,825 permits.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，並廣東鹽司及市舶提舉司為廣東鹽課市舶提舉司，每歲辦鹽一萬一千七百二十五引。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the Guangdong Salt Commission and Maritime Trade Commissionerate were merged as the Guangdong Salt Levy and Maritime Trade Commissionerate; annual salt production was eleven thousand seven hundred twenty-five permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, the Guangdong Salt Commission and Maritime Trade Commissionerate were merged into the Guangdong Salt Levy and Maritime Trade Commissionerate, with an annual quota of 11,725 permits.

sentences.zh: 大德四年，增至正余鹽二萬一千九百八十二引。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dade, it was increased to regular and surplus salt totaling twenty-one thousand nine hundred eighty-two permits.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 4 (1300), the regular and surplus salt quota was raised to 21,982 permits.

sentences.zh: 十年，又增至三萬引。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, it was again increased to thirty thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, the quota was raised again to 30,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 十一年，三萬五千五百引。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, thirty-five thousand five hundred permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, production stood at 35,500 permits.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，又增余鹽一萬五千引。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, surplus salt was again increased by fifteen thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 1 (1308), surplus salt was increased by another 15,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 延祐二年，歲煎五萬五百引。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanyou, annual boiled salt was fifty thousand one hundred permits.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 2 (1315), annual boiled salt stood at 50,100 permits.

sentences.zh: 五年，又增至五萬五百五十二引。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, it was again increased to fifty thousand one hundred fifty-two permits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, the quota was raised again to 50,152 permits.

sentences.zh: 所隸之場凡十有三。

translations.literal: The subordinate salt fields numbered thirteen in all.
translations.idiomatic: There were thirteen subordinate salt fields.

sentences.zh: 廣海之鹽：至元十三年，初立廣海鹽課提舉司，辦鹽二萬四千引。

translations.literal: Salt of Guanghai: in the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan, the Guanghai Salt Levy Commissionerate was first established; salt production was twenty-four thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: Salt in the Guanghai region: In Zhiyuan 13 (1276), the Guanghai Salt Levy Commissionerate was established, with production at 24,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 三十年，又立廣西石康鹽課提舉司。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, the Shikang Salt Levy Commissionerate in Guangxi was also established.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, the Shikang Salt Levy Commissionerate in Guangxi was also established.

sentences.zh: 大德十年，增一萬一千引。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dade, eleven thousand permits were added.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 10 (1306), production was increased by 11,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，又增余鹽一萬五千引。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, surplus salt was again increased by fifteen thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 1 (1308), surplus salt was increased by another 15,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 延祐二年，正余鹽通為五萬一百六十五引。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanyou, regular and surplus salt totaled fifty thousand one hundred sixty-five permits.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 2 (1315), regular and surplus salt combined came to 50,165 permits.

sentences.zh: 凡天下一歲總辦之數，唯天歷為可考，今並著於後：鹽，總二百五十六萬四千餘引。

translations.literal: As for the empire's total annual quota, only Tianli can be verified; they are now all recorded below: salt, in all more than two million five hundred sixty-four thousand permits.
translations.idiomatic: Empire-wide annual totals are verifiable only for the Tianli reign; they are recorded below: salt totaled just over 2,564,000 permits.

sentences.zh: 鹽課鈔，總七百六十六萬一千餘錠。

translations.literal: Salt levies in notes, in all more than seven million six hundred sixty-one thousand ingots.
translations.idiomatic: Salt levies in paper notes totaled just over 7,661,000 ingots.

sentences.zh: ○茶法

translations.literal: ○ Tea Monopoly Law
translations.idiomatic: Tea Monopoly Law

sentences.zh: 榷茶始於唐德宗，至宋遂為國賦，額與鹽等矣。

translations.literal: The tea monopoly began under Tang Dezong; by Song it had become a state levy, its quota equal to that of salt.
translations.idiomatic: The tea monopoly began under Tang Dezong; by the Song it ranked as a state levy on par with salt.

sentences.zh: 元之茶課，由約而博，大率因宋之舊而為之制焉。

translations.literal: Yuan tea levies, from modest to extensive, were for the most part fashioned after Song precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan tea levies expanded from modest beginnings, largely following Song precedent.

sentences.zh: 世祖至元五年，用運使白賡言，榷成都茶，於京兆、鞏昌置局發賣，私自采賣者，其罪與私鹽法同。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan under Emperor Shizu, on the advice of Transport Commissioner Bai Geng, Chengdu tea was monopolized; bureaus were set up at Jingzhao and Gongchang to sell it; those who gathered and sold privately were punished under the same law as for private salt.
translations.idiomatic: In Shizu's Zhiyuan 5 (1268), on Transport Commissioner Bai Geng's advice, Chengdu tea was placed under monopoly, with sales bureaus at Jingzhao and Gongchang; private gathering and sale was punished like private salt.

sentences.zh: 六年，始立西蜀四川監榷茶場使司掌之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Western Shu-Sichuan Tea Monopoly Field Commissionerate was first established to administer it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, the Western Shu-Sichuan Tea Monopoly Field Commissionerate was established to administer it.

sentences.zh: 十三年，既平宋，復用左丞呂文煥言，榷江西茶，以宋會五十貫準中統鈔一貫。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, after the Song had been pacified, on the advice of Left Chancellor Lü Wenhuan, Jiangxi tea was monopolized, with fifty strings of Song huizi converted to one string of Zhongtong notes.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, after the Song conquest, on Left Chancellor Lü Wenhuan's advice, Jiangxi tea was monopolized, converting 50 strings of Song huizi to 1 string of Zhongtong notes.

sentences.zh: 十三年，定長引短引之法，以三分取一。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, the method of long permits and short permits was fixed, taking one third.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, long-permit and short-permit regulations were fixed at one third.

sentences.zh: 長引每引計茶一百二十斤，收鈔五錢四分二厘八毫。

translations.literal: Each long permit counted one hundred twenty jin of tea and collected five qian four fen two li eight hao in notes.
translations.idiomatic: Each long permit covered 120 jin of tea and collected 5 qian 4 fen 2 li 8 hao in notes.

sentences.zh: 短引計茶九十斤，收鈔四錢二分八毫。

translations.literal: Each short permit counted ninety jin of tea and collected four qian two fen eight hao in notes.
translations.idiomatic: Each short permit covered 90 jin of tea and collected 4 qian 2 fen 8 hao in notes.

sentences.zh: 是歲，征一千二百餘錠。

translations.literal: That year, more than one thousand two hundred ingots were collected.
translations.idiomatic: That year, collections exceeded 1,200 ingots.

sentences.zh: 十四年，取三分之半，增至二千三百餘錠。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, taking half of one third, it was increased to more than two thousand three hundred ingots.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, raising the rate to half of one third, collections rose to over 2,300 ingots.

sentences.zh: 十五年，又增至六千六百餘錠。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, it was again increased to more than six thousand six hundred ingots.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, collections rose again to over 6,600 ingots.

sentences.zh: 十七年，置榷茶都轉運司於江州，總江淮、荊湖、福廣之稅，而遂除長引，專用短引。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, the Tea Monopoly Metropolitan Transport Commission was established at Jiangzhou to oversee levies in the Jiang-Huai, Jing-Hu, and Fu-Guang regions; long permits were then abolished and short permits alone were used.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, the Tea Monopoly Metropolitan Transport Commission was established at Jiangzhou to oversee Jiang-Huai, Jing-Hu, and Fu-Guang levies; long permits were abolished in favor of short permits alone.

sentences.zh: 每引收鈔二兩四錢五分，草茶每引收鈔二兩二錢四分。

translations.literal: Each permit collected two liang four qian five fen in notes; coarse tea per permit collected two liang two qian four fen.
translations.idiomatic: Each permit collected 2 liang 4 qian 5 fen in notes; coarse tea permits collected 2 liang 2 qian 4 fen.

sentences.zh: 十八年，增額至二萬四千錠。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, the quota was increased to twenty-four thousand ingots.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, the quota rose to 24,000 ingots.

sentences.zh: 十九年，以江南茶課官為置局，令客買引，通行貨賣。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, because Jiangnan tea levies were handled by officials who set up bureaus, merchants were ordered to buy permits and sell tea freely.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, with Jiangnan tea levies handled through official bureaus, merchants were required to buy permits for unrestricted trade.

sentences.zh: 歲終，增二萬錠。

translations.literal: By year's end, it increased by twenty thousand ingots.
translations.idiomatic: By year's end, collections had risen by 20,000 ingots.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，廉運使言：「各處食茶課程，抑配於民，非便。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Transport Commissioner Lian said: "Tea levies for tea consumption in various places, forcibly apportioned to the people, are inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, Transport Commissioner Lian reported: "Forcing tea-consumption levies onto households in various places is burdensome.

sentences.zh: 」於是革之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " The practice was then abolished.

sentences.zh: 而以其所革之數，於正課每引增一兩五分，通為三兩五錢。

translations.literal: The amount thus abolished was added to the regular levy at one liang five fen per permit, making three liang five qian in all.
translations.idiomatic: The abolished amount was folded into the regular levy, raising each permit by 1 liang 5 fen to 3 liang 5 qian total.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，又以李起南言，增為五貫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, on the advice of Li Qinan, it was again increased to five strings.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, on Li Qinan's advice, the rate was raised to 5 strings.

sentences.zh: 是年征四萬錠。

translations.literal: That year, forty thousand ingots were collected.
translations.idiomatic: That year, collections came to 40,000 ingots.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，改立江西等處都轉運司。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, the Jiangxi Metropolitan Transport Commission was reorganized.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, the Jiangxi Metropolitan Transport Commission was reorganized.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，丞相桑哥增引稅為一十貫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, Chancellor Sangge increased the permit tax to ten strings.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, Chancellor Sangge raised the permit tax to 10 strings.

sentences.zh: 三十年，又改江南茶法。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, the Jiangnan tea law was again revised.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, the Jiangnan tea law was revised again.

sentences.zh: 凡管茶提舉司一十六所，罷其課少者五所，並入附近提舉司。

translations.literal: In all there were sixteen tea commissionerates under administration; five with smaller levies were abolished and merged into nearby commissionerates.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen tea commissionerates were under administration; five low-yield offices were abolished and merged into nearby ones.

sentences.zh: 每茶商貨茶，必令賫引，無引者與私茶同。

translations.literal: Whenever tea merchants shipped tea, they were required to carry permits; those without permits were treated like private tea.
translations.idiomatic: Tea merchants were required to carry permits; those without were treated as smugglers.

sentences.zh: 引之外，又有茶由，以給賣零茶者。

translations.literal: Beyond permits, there were also tea slips to supply those who sold tea in small quantities.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond full permits, tea slips were issued for retail sellers.

sentences.zh: 初，每由茶九斤，收鈔一兩，至是自三斤至三十斤分為十等，隨處批引局同，每引收鈔一錢。

translations.literal: At first, each slip for nine jin of tea collected one liang in notes; from then on, from three jin to thirty jin were divided into ten grades, the same at permit-verification offices everywhere; each permit collected one qian in notes.
translations.idiomatic: Initially each slip for 9 jin of tea cost 1 liang in notes; thereafter tea from 3 to 30 jin was divided into ten grades, uniform at all permit offices, with each permit collecting 1 qian.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年有獻利者言：「舊法江南茶商至江北者又稅之，其在江南賣者，亦宜更稅，如江北之制。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen, a profit-seeker said: "Under the old law, Jiangnan tea merchants going to Jiangbei were taxed again; those selling within Jiangnan should also be taxed anew, as under the Jiangbei system.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanzhen 1 (1295), a profit-seeker proposed: "Under the old law, Jiangnan tea merchants shipping to Jiangbei paid a second tax; sales within Jiangnan should be taxed similarly to Jiangbei.

sentences.zh: 」於是朝議復增江南課三千錠，而弗稅。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the court deliberated and again increased the Jiangnan levy by three thousand ingots, but did not impose the tax.
translations.idiomatic: " The court instead raised the Jiangnan levy by 3,000 ingots without imposing the new tax.

sentences.zh: 是年凡征八萬三千錠。

translations.literal: That year, eighty-three thousand ingots were collected in all.
translations.idiomatic: That year, total collections came to 83,000 ingots.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，以龍興、瑞州為皇太后湯沐邑，其課入徽政院。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, Longxing and Ruizhou were made fiefs for the empress dowager's maintenance; their levies went to the Office of Imperial Administration.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 1 (1308), Longxing and Ruizhou became the empress dowager's maintenance fiefs, with levies assigned to the Office of Imperial Administration.

sentences.zh: 四年，增額至一十七萬一千一百三十一錠。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the quota was increased to one hundred seventy-one thousand one hundred thirty-one ingots.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, the quota rose to 171,131 ingots.

sentences.zh: 皇慶二年，更定江南茶法，又增至一十九萬二千八百六十六錠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangqing, the Jiangnan tea law was again revised, and it was increased to one hundred ninety-two thousand eight hundred sixty-six ingots.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangqing 2 (1313), the Jiangnan tea law was revised again, raising collections to 192,866 ingots.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，改設批驗茶由局官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou, officials for permit-verification and tea-slip bureaus were reorganized.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 1 (1314), permit-verification and tea-slip bureau officials were reorganized.

sentences.zh: 五年，用江西茶副法忽魯丁言，立減引添課之法，每引增稅為一十二兩五錢，通辦鈔二十五萬錠。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, on the advice of Jiangxi Tea Vice-Commissioner Fa Huluding, a method of reducing permits while adding levies was established; the added tax per permit was twelve liang five qian, with a combined quota of two hundred fifty thousand ingots in notes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, on Jiangxi Tea Vice-Commissioner Fa Huluding's advice, a system of fewer permits with higher levies was adopted: an added 12 liang 5 qian per permit, for a combined quota of 250,000 ingots.

sentences.zh: 七年，遂增至二十八萬九千二百一十一錠。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, it was increased to two hundred eighty-nine thousand two hundred eleven ingots.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, collections rose to 289,211 ingots.

sentences.zh: 天歷二年，始罷榷司而歸諸州縣，其歲征之數，蓋與延祐同。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianli, the monopoly commission was first abolished and authority returned to prefectures and counties; the annual collection was about the same as under Yanyou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 2 (1329), the monopoly commission was abolished and authority returned to prefectures and counties; annual collections remained roughly at Yanyou levels.

sentences.zh: 至順之後，無籍可考。

translations.literal: After Zhishun, no records can be verified.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhishun (1330), no reliable records survive.

sentences.zh: 他如範殿帥茶、西番大葉茶、建寧胯茶，亦無從知其始末，故皆不著。

translations.literal: Other cases such as Fandianshuai tea, Western Regions large-leaf tea, and Jianning kua tea also cannot be traced from beginning to end, and so are not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Other varieties such as Fandianshuai tea, Western Regions large-leaf tea, and Jianning kua tea cannot be traced from start to finish and are omitted.

sentences.zh: ○酒醋課

translations.literal: ○ Wine and Vinegar Levies
translations.idiomatic: Wine and Vinegar Levies

sentences.zh: 元之有酒醋課，自太宗始。

translations.literal: Yuan wine and vinegar levies began under Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan wine and vinegar levies began under Taizong.

sentences.zh: 其後皆著定額，為國賦之一焉，利之所入亦厚矣。

translations.literal: Thereafter fixed quotas were established; they were one of the state levies, and the revenue they yielded was also substantial.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter fixed quotas were established as a major state revenue source yielding substantial income.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗辛卯年，立酒醋務坊場官，榷沽辦課，仍以各州府司縣長官充提點官，隸征收課稅所，其課額驗民戶多寡定之。

translations.literal: At first, in Taizong's xinmao year, wine and vinegar bureau and workshop officials were established to monopolize sales and collect levies; the chief officials of each prefecture, circuit, and county still served as intendant officials, subordinate to the Tax Collection Office; levy quotas were fixed according to the number of households.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, in Taizong's xinmao year (1231), wine and vinegar bureau officials were appointed to monopolize sales and collect levies, with prefecture, circuit, and county chiefs serving as intendants under the Tax Collection Office; quotas were set by household count.

sentences.zh: 甲午年，頒酒曲醋貨條禁，私造者依條治罪。

translations.literal: In the jiawu year, regulations prohibiting private manufacture of wine yeast and vinegar goods were promulgated; private makers were punished according to the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiawu year (1234), regulations banning private manufacture of wine yeast and vinegar were promulgated, with violators punished accordingly.

sentences.zh: 世祖至元十六年，以大都、河間、山東酒醋商稅等課並入鹽運司。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan under Emperor Shizu, wine, vinegar, and commercial tax levies in Dadu, Hejian, and Shandong were merged into the Salt Transport Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In Shizu's Zhiyuan 16 (1279), wine, vinegar, and commercial tax levies in Dadu, Hejian, and Shandong were placed under the Salt Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，詔免農民醋課。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, an edict remitted farmers' vinegar levies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, an edict remitted farmers' vinegar levies.

sentences.zh: 是年二月，命隨路酒課依京師例，每石取一十兩。

translations.literal: In the second month of that year, it was ordered that wine levies in each circuit follow the capital precedent, taking ten liang per shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of that year, wine levies in each circuit were ordered to follow the capital rate of 10 liang per shi.

sentences.zh: 三月，用右丞盧世榮等言，罷上都醋課，其酒課亦改榷沽之制，令酒戶自具工本，官司拘賣，每石止輸鈔五兩。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the advice of Right Chancellor Lu Shirong and others, the Shangdu vinegar levy was abolished; the wine levy also changed to a monopoly system, ordering wine households to supply their own capital while the government controlled sales, paying only five liang in notes per shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on Right Chancellor Lu Shirong's advice, the Shangdu vinegar levy was abolished and wine was placed under monopoly: wine households supplied capital while the government controlled sales at 5 liang in notes per shi.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，詔江西酒醋之課不隸茶運司，福建酒醋之課不隸鹽運司，皆依舊令有司辦之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, an edict declared that Jiangxi wine and vinegar levies were not subordinate to the Tea Transport Commission, and Fujian wine and vinegar levies were not subordinate to the Salt Transport Commission; all were to be handled as before by the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year, an edict restored Jiangxi wine and vinegar levies to local control rather than the Tea Transport Commission, and Fujian wine and vinegar levies to local control rather than the Salt Transport Commission.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，丞相完澤等言：「杭州省酒課歲辦二十七萬餘錠，湖廣、龍興歲辦止九萬錠，輕重不均。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Chancellor Wanze and others said: "The Hangzhou Branch Secretariat's annual wine levy is more than two hundred seventy thousand ingots, while Huguang and Longxing together furnish only ninety thousand ingots—the burden is uneven.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, Chancellor Wanze reported: "Hangzhou's annual wine levy exceeds 270,000 ingots, while Huguang and Longxing together pay only 90,000—the burden is uneven.

sentences.zh: 」於是減杭州省十分之二，令湖廣、龍興、南京三省分辦。

translations.literal: " Thereupon two tenths were cut from the Hangzhou Branch Secretariat, and Huguang, Longxing, and Nanjing provinces were ordered to share the quota.
translations.idiomatic: " Hangzhou's quota was cut by two tenths, with Huguang, Longxing, and Nanjing provinces assigned to share the load.

sentences.zh: 大德八年，大都酒課提舉司設槽房一百所。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dade, the Dadu Wine Levy Commissionerate established one hundred fermenting houses.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 8 (1304), the Dadu Wine Levy Commissionerate established 100 fermenting houses.

sentences.zh: 九年，並為三十所，每所一日所醞，不許過二十五石之上。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, they were consolidated into thirty houses; each house's daily brewing was not permitted to exceed twenty-five shi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, they were consolidated to 30 houses, each limited to 25 shi of daily brewing.

sentences.zh: 十年，復增三所。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, three houses were again added.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, 3 more houses were added.

sentences.zh: 至大三年，又增為五十四所。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhidao, they were again increased to fifty-four houses.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 3 (1310), the total rose again to 54 houses.

sentences.zh: 其制之可考者如此。

translations.literal: The system as it can be verified was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the system as far as records allow.

sentences.zh: 若夫累朝以課程撥賜諸王公主及各寺者，凡九所云。

translations.literal: As for levies allocated and granted to princes, princesses, and various temples across successive reigns, there were nine establishments in all, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Levy allocations granted to princes, princesses, and temples across successive reigns numbered nine establishments in all.

sentences.zh: 天下每歲總入之數：酒課：腹裏，五萬六千二百四十三錠六十七兩一錢。

translations.literal: The empire's total annual receipts: wine levies: in the heartland, fifty-six thousand two hundred forty-three ingots sixty-seven liang one qian.
translations.idiomatic: Empire-wide annual receipts—wine levies: heartland territories, 56,243 ingots 67 liang 1 qian.

sentences.zh: 遼陽行省，二千二百五十錠一十一兩二錢。

translations.literal: Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, two thousand two hundred fifty ingots eleven liang two qian.
translations.idiomatic: Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, 2,250 ingots 11 liang 2 qian.

sentences.zh: 河南行省，七萬五千七十七錠一十一兩五錢。

translations.literal: Henan Branch Secretariat, seventy-five thousand seventy-seven ingots eleven liang five qian.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Branch Secretariat, 75,077 ingots 11 liang 5 qian.

sentences.zh: 陜西行省，一萬一千七百七十四錠三十四兩四錢。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, eleven thousand seven hundred seventy-four ingots thirty-four liang four qian.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, 11,774 ingots 34 liang 4 qian.

sentences.zh: 四川行省，七千五百九十錠二十兩。

translations.literal: Sichuan Branch Secretariat, seven thousand five hundred ninety ingots twenty liang.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan Branch Secretariat, 7,590 ingots 20 liang.

sentences.zh: 甘肅行省，二千七十八錠三十五兩九錢。

translations.literal: Gansu Branch Secretariat, two thousand seventy-eight ingots thirty-five liang nine qian.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu Branch Secretariat, 2,078 ingots 35 liang 9 qian.

sentences.zh: 雲南行省，<貝八>二十萬一千一百一十七索。

translations.literal: Yunnan Branch Secretariat, <貝八> two hundred one thousand one hundred seventeen suo.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan Branch Secretariat, 201,117 suo of shell currency.

sentences.zh: 江浙行省，一十九萬六千六百五十四錠二十一兩三錢。

translations.literal: Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, one hundred ninety-six thousand six hundred fifty-four ingots twenty-one liang three qian.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, 196,654 ingots 21 liang 3 qian.

sentences.zh: 江西行省，五萬八千六百四十錠一十六兩八錢。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, fifty-eight thousand six hundred forty ingots sixteen liang eight qian.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, 58,640 ingots 16 liang 8 qian.

sentences.zh: 湖廣行省，五萬八千八百四十八錠四十九兩八錢。

translations.literal: Huguang Branch Secretariat, fifty-eight thousand eight hundred forty-eight ingots forty-nine liang eight qian.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang Branch Secretariat, 58,848 ingots 49 liang 8 qian.

sentences.zh: 醋課：腹裏，三千五百七十六錠四十八兩九錢。

translations.literal: Vinegar levies: in the heartland, three thousand five hundred seventy-six ingots forty-eight liang nine qian.
translations.idiomatic: Vinegar levies—heartland territories, 3,576 ingots 48 liang 9 qian.

sentences.zh: 遼陽行省，三十四錠二十六兩五錢。

translations.literal: Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, thirty-four ingots twenty-six liang five qian.
translations.idiomatic: Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, 34 ingots 26 liang 5 qian.

sentences.zh: 河南行省，二千七百四十錠三十六兩四錢。

translations.literal: Henan Branch Secretariat, two thousand seven hundred forty ingots thirty-six liang four qian.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Branch Secretariat, 2,740 ingots 36 liang 4 qian.

sentences.zh: 陜西行省，一千五百七十三錠三十九兩二錢。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, one thousand five hundred seventy-three ingots thirty-nine liang two qian.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, 1,573 ingots 39 liang 2 qian.

sentences.zh: 四川行省，六百一十六錠一十二兩八錢。

translations.literal: Sichuan Branch Secretariat, six hundred sixteen ingots twelve liang eight qian.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan Branch Secretariat, 616 ingots 12 liang 8 qian.

sentences.zh: 江浙行省，一萬一千八百七十錠一十九兩六錢。

translations.literal: Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, eleven thousand eight hundred seventy ingots nineteen liang six qian.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, 11,870 ingots 19 liang 6 qian.

sentences.zh: 江西行省，九百五十一錠二十四兩五錢。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, nine hundred fifty-one ingots twenty-four liang five qian.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, 951 ingots 24 liang 5 qian.

sentences.zh: 湖廣行省，一千二百三十一錠二十七兩九錢。

translations.literal: Huguang Branch Secretariat, one thousand two hundred thirty-one ingots twenty-seven liang nine qian.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang Branch Secretariat, 1,231 ingots 27 liang 9 qian.

sentences.zh: ○商稅

translations.literal: ○ Commercial Tax
translations.idiomatic: Commercial Tax

sentences.zh: 商賈之有稅，本以抑末，而國用亦資焉。

translations.literal: Taxes on merchants and traders were originally meant to restrain the secondary occupation, yet state revenue also drew upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes on merchants were originally meant to restrain commerce, yet they also supplied state revenue.

sentences.zh: 元初，未有定制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuan, no fixed system existed.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yuan founding, no fixed system existed.

sentences.zh: 太宗甲午年，始立征收課稅所，凡倉庫院務官並合幹人等，命各處官司選有產有行之人充之。

translations.literal: In Taizong's jiawu year, the Tax Collection Office was first established; for warehouse and workshop officials and their clerks, each local office was ordered to select men of property and standing to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's jiawu year (1234), the Tax Collection Office was established; warehouse and workshop officials and clerks were to be selected from men of property and standing.

sentences.zh: 其所辦課程，每月赴所輸納。

translations.literal: The levies they handled were delivered monthly to the office.
translations.idiomatic: Levies collected were delivered monthly to the office.

sentences.zh: 有貿易借貸者，並徒二年，杖七十；

translations.literal: Those who engaged in trade or lending were alike sentenced to two years of penal servitude and seventy blows;
translations.idiomatic: Those who engaged in trade or lending faced two years' penal servitude and 70 blows;

sentences.zh: 所官擾民取財者，其罪亦如之。

translations.literal: office officials who harassed the people and took money were punished likewise.
translations.idiomatic: office officials who extorted the people were punished the same way.

sentences.zh: 世祖中統四年，用阿合馬、王光祖等言，凡在京權勢之家為商賈，及以官銀賣買之人，並令赴務輸稅，入城不吊引者同匿稅法。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhongtong under Emperor Shizu, on the advice of Ahmad and Wang Guangzu, all powerful families in the capital who acted as merchants, and those who traded with official silver, were ordered to pay tax at the workshop; those entering the city without displaying permits were treated under the law for concealing tax.
translations.idiomatic: In Shizu's Zhongtong 4 (1263), on Ahmad and Wang Guangzu's advice, powerful capital families trading as merchants and those dealing in official silver were required to pay tax at the workshop; entering the city without a permit counted as tax evasion.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，遂定三十分取一之制，以銀四萬五千錠為額，有溢額者別作增余。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan, the system of one part in thirty was then fixed, with a quota of forty-five thousand ingots of silver; surpluses were handled separately as surplus revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 7 (1270), a one-thirtieth rate was fixed with a quota of 45,000 ingots of silver; surpluses were recorded separately.

sentences.zh: 是年五月，以上都商旅往來艱辛，特免其課。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of that year, because merchants traveling to and from Shangdu faced hardship, their levies were specially remitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of that year, Shangdu merchants' levies were specially remitted because of the hardships of travel.

sentences.zh: 凡典賣田宅不納稅者，禁之。

translations.literal: All who sold or mortgaged fields and houses without paying tax were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Sale or mortgage of fields and houses without paying tax was forbidden.

sentences.zh: 二十年，詔各路課程，差廉幹官二員提調，增羨者遷賞，虧兌者陪償降黜。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, an edict ordered that in each circuit two upright and capable officials be assigned to supervise levies; those who increased collections were promoted and rewarded, while those who fell short made restitution and were demoted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, each circuit was ordered to assign two capable officials to supervise levies; surplus collectors were promoted, shortfalls required restitution and demotion.

sentences.zh: 凡隨路所辦，每月以其數申部，違期不申及雖申不圓者，其首領官初犯罰俸，再犯決一十七，令史加一等，三犯正官取招呈省。

translations.literal: Whatever each circuit handled was reported monthly to the ministry; those who failed to report on time, or whose reports were incomplete, had their chief official fined salary on the first offense, beaten seventeen blows on the second, with clerks punished one grade higher; on the third offense the chief official was interrogated and reported to the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit reported monthly to the ministry; late or incomplete reports brought salary fines for chiefs on first offense, 17 blows on second (clerks one grade higher), and interrogation and report to the secretariat on third.

sentences.zh: 其院務官俸鈔，於增余錢內給之。

translations.literal: The salary notes of workshop officials were paid from surplus revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Workshop officials' salaries were paid from surplus revenue.

sentences.zh: 是年，始定上都稅課六十分取一；

translations.literal: That year, the Shangdu tax levy of one part in sixty was first fixed;
translations.idiomatic: That year, Shangdu's one-sixtieth tax rate was first established;

sentences.zh: 舊城市肆院務遷入都城者，四十分取一。

translations.literal: for old city market workshops moved into the capital, one part in forty.
translations.idiomatic: for old city market workshops relocated to the capital, one fortieth.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，又增商稅契本，每一道為中統鈔三錢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, commercial tax deed certificates were again increased; each document was set at three qian of Zhongtong notes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, the commercial tax on deed certificates was raised again to three qian of Zhongtong paper money per document.

sentences.zh: 減上都稅課，於一百兩之中取七錢半。

translations.literal: Shangdu tax levies were reduced: from every hundred liang, seven qian and a half were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Shangdu's tax levy was reduced to seven and a half qian per hundred liang.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，從丞相桑哥之請，遂大增天下商稅，腹裏為二十萬錠，江南為二十五萬錠。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, at Grand Councillor Sangge's request, commercial taxes empire-wide were then greatly increased; the inner territories were set at two hundred thousand ingots, Jiangnan at two hundred fifty thousand ingots.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, at Grand Councillor Sangge's request, commercial taxes were sharply raised across the empire: 200,000 ingots for the inner territories and 250,000 for Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，定諸路輸納之限，不許過四孟月十五日。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, payment deadlines for each circuit were fixed; delivery was not permitted after the fifteenth day of the four meng months.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, each circuit's payment deadline was fixed: no remittance was allowed after the fifteenth day of the four seasonal opening months.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，詔天下商稅有增余者，毋作額。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, an edict declared that wherever commercial tax produced surplus revenue, it should not be counted toward the quota.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, an edict ordered that commercial tax surpluses empire-wide should not be folded into the official quota.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，用平章剌真言，又增上都之稅。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen, on Pingzhang Lachin's advice, Shangdu taxes were again increased.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanzhen 1 (1295), on Vice Grand Councillor Lachin's advice, Shangdu taxes were raised again.

sentences.zh: ○市舶

translations.literal: ○ Maritime Trade
translations.idiomatic: Maritime Trade

sentences.zh: 互市之法，自漢通南粵始，其後歷代皆嘗行之，至宋置市舶司於浙、廣之地，以通諸蕃貨易，則其制為益詳矣。

translations.literal: The method of frontier exchange trade began when Han opened relations with Nanyue; later dynasties all tried it at times. By the Song, Maritime Trade Commissionerates were placed in Zhejiang and Guangdong to trade with foreign countries, and the system grew ever more detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier exchange trade began when the Han opened relations with Nanyue; later dynasties all experimented with it. Under the Song, Maritime Trade Commissionerates in Zhejiang and Guangdong regulated trade with foreign lands, and the system grew ever more elaborate.

sentences.zh: 元自世祖定江南，凡鄰海諸郡與蕃國往還互易舶貨者，其貨以十分取一，粗者十五分取一，以市舶官主之。

translations.literal: After the Yuan's Shizu pacified Jiangnan, for all coastal circuits that exchanged ship-borne goods with foreign countries, fine goods were taxed one part in ten, coarse goods one part in fifteen, supervised by maritime trade officials.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizu pacified Jiangnan, coastal circuits trading shipborne goods with foreign countries paid one-tenth on fine goods and one-fifteenth on coarse goods, under maritime trade officials.

sentences.zh: 其發舶回帆，必著其所至之地，驗其所易之物，給以公文，為之期日，大抵皆因宋舊制而為之法焉。

translations.literal: When ships departed or returned, they had to record their destinations, have exchanged goods inspected, and receive official documents with set deadlines—in general all following the Song system as law.
translations.idiomatic: Departing and returning ships had to declare their destinations, have traded goods inspected, and receive dated official permits—largely following the old Song regulations.

sentences.zh: 於是至元十四年，立市舶司一於泉州，令忙古兒領之。

translations.literal: Thus in the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, one Maritime Trade Commissionerate was established at Quanzhou, with Mangghul placed in charge.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 14 (1277), a Maritime Trade Commissionerate was established at Quanzhou under Mangghul.

sentences.zh: 立市舶司三於慶元、上海、澉浦，令福建安撫使楊發督之。

translations.literal: Three Maritime Trade Commissionerates were established at Qingyuan, Shanghai, and Ganpu, supervised by Fujian Pacification Commissioner Yang Fa.
translations.idiomatic: Three Maritime Trade Commissionerates were set up at Qingyuan, Shanghai, and Ganpu, overseen by Fujian Pacification Commissioner Yang Fa.

sentences.zh: 每歲招集舶商，於蕃邦博易珠翠香貨等物。

translations.literal: Each year merchant ships were summoned to trade in foreign lands for pearls, jade, incense, and other luxuries.
translations.idiomatic: Each year merchant fleets were summoned to trade abroad for pearls, jade, incense, and other luxuries.

sentences.zh: 及次年回帆，依例抽解，然後聽其貨賣。

translations.literal: When they returned the next year, proportional shares were extracted according to regulation before they were permitted to sell.
translations.idiomatic: On their return the following year, proportional shares were taken as prescribed before goods could be sold.

sentences.zh: 時客船自泉、福販土產之物者，其所征亦與蕃貨等，上海市舶司提控王楠以為言，於是定雙抽、單抽之制。

translations.literal: At that time, passenger ships from Quanzhou and Fuzhou trading local products were taxed at the same rate as foreign goods. Wang Nan, controller of the Shanghai Maritime Trade Commissionerate, raised the matter, and the systems of double extraction and single extraction were then fixed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, ships from Quanzhou and Fuzhou carrying local goods were taxed like foreign cargo. Wang Nan, controller at the Shanghai Maritime Trade Commissionerate, protested, and the double- and single-extraction rates were then fixed.

sentences.zh: 雙抽者蕃貨也，單抽者土貨也。

translations.literal: Double extraction applied to foreign goods; single extraction to local goods.
translations.idiomatic: Double extraction applied to foreign goods; single extraction to local goods.

sentences.zh: 十九年，又用耿左丞言，以鈔易銅錢，令市舶司以錢易海外金珠貨物，仍聽舶戶通販抽分。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, again following Vice Councillor Geng's advice, paper notes were exchanged for copper coins; Maritime Trade Commissionerates were ordered to use coins to purchase overseas gold, pearls, and goods, while still allowing ship owners to trade broadly under proportional extraction.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, again on Vice Councillor Geng's advice, paper money was exchanged for copper cash; Maritime Trade Commissionerates were to use cash to buy overseas gold, pearls, and goods, while ship owners could still trade freely under proportional extraction.

sentences.zh: 二十年，遂定抽分之法。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, the proportional extraction system was then fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, the proportional extraction system was formally established.

sentences.zh: 是年十月，忙古兒言，舶商皆以金銀易香木，於是下令禁之，唯鐵不禁。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year, Mangghul reported that merchant ships all used gold and silver to buy fragrant woods; an order was then issued forbidding this—only iron was not forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year, Mangghul reported that merchants were using gold and silver to buy fragrant woods; an order forbade this—only iron was exempt.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，設市舶都轉運司於杭、泉二州，官自具船、給本，選人入蕃，貿易諸貨。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, a Metropolitan Maritime Trade Transport Commission was established at Hangzhou and Quanzhou; the government supplied its own ships and capital, selected men to enter foreign lands, and traded all sorts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, a Metropolitan Maritime Trade Transport Commission was set up at Hangzhou and Quanzhou; the state furnished ships and capital, sent men abroad, and traded all manner of goods.

sentences.zh: 其所獲之息，以十分為率，官取其七，所易人得其三。

translations.literal: Of the profit obtained, by a rate of ten parts the government took seven and the traders took three.
translations.idiomatic: Profits were split on a ten-part basis: seven parts to the state and three to the traders.

sentences.zh: 凡權勢之家，皆不得用己錢入蕃為賈，犯者罪之，仍籍其家產之半。

translations.literal: No powerful family might use its own money to enter foreign lands as merchants; violators were punished and half their household property was confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families were forbidden to invest private funds in foreign trade; violators were punished and half their property was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 其諸蕃客旅就官船賣買者，依例抽之。

translations.literal: Foreign merchants and travelers who bought and sold with official ships were proportionally taxed according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign merchants who traded with official ships were taxed proportionally as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，並福建市舶司入鹽運司，改曰都轉運司，領福建漳、泉鹽貨市舶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, the Fujian Maritime Trade Commissionerate was merged into the Salt Transport Commission, renamed the Metropolitan Transport Commission, overseeing Fujian Zhangzhou and Quanzhou salt goods and maritime trade.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, the Fujian Maritime Trade Commissionerate was merged into the Salt Transport Commission as the Metropolitan Transport Commission, overseeing salt, goods, and maritime trade in Zhangzhou and Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，禁海外博易者，毋用銅錢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, those trading overseas were forbidden to use copper coins.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, overseas traders were forbidden to use copper cash.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，又禁廣州官民，毋得運米至占城諸蕃出糶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Guangzhou officials and populace were again forbidden to transport grain to Champa and other foreign countries for sale.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, Guangzhou officials and commoners were again forbidden to ship grain to Champa and other foreign lands for sale.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，命市舶驗貨抽分。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, Maritime Trade Commissionerates were ordered to inspect goods and extract proportional shares.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, Maritime Trade Commissionerates were ordered to inspect cargo and take proportional shares.

sentences.zh: 是年十一月，中書省定抽分之數及漏稅之法。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year, the Central Secretariat fixed the rates of proportional extraction and methods for concealed-tax offenses.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year, the Central Secretariat fixed extraction rates and penalties for concealed taxes.

sentences.zh: 凡商旅販泉、福等處已抽之物，於本省有市舶司之地賣者，細色於二十五分之中取一，粗色於三十分之中取一，免其輸稅。

translations.literal: Whenever merchants sold goods already proportionally extracted at Quanzhou, Fuzhou, and other places in a province with a Maritime Trade Commissionerate, fine goods paid one part in twenty-five, coarse goods one part in thirty, and were exempt from further tax.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants reselling goods already taxed at Quanzhou, Fuzhou, or elsewhere within a province that had a Maritime Trade Commissionerate paid one twenty-fifth on fine goods and one thirtieth on coarse goods, and owed no further tax.

sentences.zh: 其就市舶司買者，止於賣處收稅，而不再抽。

translations.literal: Those who purchased at a Maritime Trade Commissionerate paid tax only at the place of sale and were not proportionally taxed again.
translations.idiomatic: Buyers at a Maritime Trade Commissionerate paid tax only at the point of sale and were not taxed again.

sentences.zh: 漏舶物貨，依例斷沒。

translations.literal: Smuggled ship goods were confiscated according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Smuggled ship cargo was confiscated as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 三十年，又定市舶抽分雜禁，凡二十二條，條多不能盡載，擇其要者錄焉。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, miscellaneous prohibitions on maritime trade proportional extraction were again fixed—twenty-two articles in all; most cannot be fully recorded, and only the essentials are set down here.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year, twenty-two miscellaneous rules on maritime extraction were fixed; most cannot all be recorded, and only the essentials are noted here.

sentences.zh: 泉州、上海、澉浦、溫州、廣東、杭州、慶元市舶司凡七所，獨泉州於抽分之外，又取三十分之一以為稅。

translations.literal: There were seven Maritime Trade Commissionerates at Quanzhou, Shanghai, Ganpu, Wenzhou, Guangdong, Hangzhou, and Qingyuan. Only Quanzhou, beyond proportional extraction, also took one thirtieth as tax.
translations.idiomatic: There were seven Maritime Trade Commissionerates: Quanzhou, Shanghai, Ganpu, Wenzhou, Guangdong, Hangzhou, and Qingyuan. Only Quanzhou, beyond proportional extraction, also levied an additional one-thirtieth as tax.

sentences.zh: 自今諸處，悉依泉州例取之，仍以溫州市舶司並入慶元，杭州市舶司並入稅務。

translations.literal: From now on all places were to follow the Quanzhou precedent; meanwhile the Wenzhou Maritime Trade Commissionerate was merged into Qingyuan, and the Hangzhou Maritime Trade Commissionerate into the Tax Office.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth all offices were to follow Quanzhou's example; the Wenzhou Maritime Trade Commissionerate was merged into Qingyuan, and Hangzhou's into the Tax Office.

sentences.zh: 凡金銀銅鐵男女，並不許私販入蕃。

translations.literal: Gold, silver, copper, iron, and men and women alike were not permitted to be privately traded into foreign lands.
translations.idiomatic: Gold, silver, copper, iron, and persons alike were forbidden from private export to foreign lands.

sentences.zh: 行省行泉府司、市舶司官，每年於回帆之時，皆前期至抽解之所，以待舶船之至，先封其堵，以次抽分，違期及作弊者罪之。

translations.literal: Each year when ships returned, provincial officials, Quanfu Bureau officials, and Maritime Trade Commissionerate officers all arrived early at the extraction site to await the ships; cargo holds were first sealed, then shares were extracted in order; those late or cheating were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Each year at the return season, provincial officials, Quanfu Bureau officers, and Maritime Trade Commissionerate staff arrived early at the extraction site, sealed holds in order, and took proportional shares; lateness or fraud was punished.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，成宗詔有司勿拘海舶，聽其自便。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, Emperor Chengzong ordered officials not to restrict merchant ships and to let them proceed freely.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, Emperor Chengzong ordered officials not to restrain merchant ships and to let them come and go freely.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，以舶船至岸，隱漏物貨者多，命就海中逆而閱之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen, because many ships concealing goods when reaching shore, an order was issued to inspect them at sea in advance.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanzhen 1 (1295), because many ships concealed cargo on arrival, officials were ordered to inspect them at sea before they reached shore.

sentences.zh: 二年，禁海商以細貨於馬八兒、唄喃、梵答剌亦納三蕃國交易，別出鈔五萬錠，令沙不丁等議規運之法。

translations.literal: In the second year, maritime merchants were forbidden to trade fine goods at the three foreign countries of Ma'bar, Peyn, and Fanjala'ina; fifty thousand ingots of notes were separately allocated and Shi Budding and others were ordered to deliberate on regulated transport methods.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, maritime merchants were forbidden to trade fine goods at Ma'bar, Peyn, and Fanjala'ina; 50,000 ingots of paper money were set aside and Shi Budding and others were ordered to devise a regulated shipping system.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，罷行泉府司。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade, the Quanfu Bureau was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 1 (1297), the Quanfu Bureau was abolished.

sentences.zh: 二年，並澉浦、上海入慶元市舶提舉司，直隸中書省。

translations.literal: In the second year, Ganpu and Shanghai were merged into the Qingyuan Maritime Trade Intendant Office, directly under the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Ganpu and Shanghai were merged into the Qingyuan Maritime Trade Intendant Office, placed directly under the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是年，又置制用院，七年，以禁商下海罷之。

translations.literal: That same year, the Directorate of Imperial Use was also established; in the seventh year it was abolished because merchant voyages to sea were forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Directorate of Imperial Use was also established; in the seventh year it was abolished when private voyages were banned.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，復立泉府院，整治市舶司事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida, the Quanfu Directorate was re-established to regulate Maritime Trade Commissionerate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 1 (1308), the Quanfu Directorate was re-established to oversee maritime trade affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年，罷行泉府院，以市舶提舉司隸行省。

translations.literal: In the second year, the Quanfu Directorate was abolished and Maritime Trade Intendant Offices were placed under branch secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, the Quanfu Directorate was abolished and Maritime Trade Intendant Offices were placed under branch secretariats.

sentences.zh: 四年，又罷之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, it was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, it was abolished again.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，復立市舶提舉司，仍禁人下蕃，官自發船貿易，回帆之日，細物十分抽二，粗物十五分抽二。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou, Maritime Trade Intendant Offices were re-established; private voyages to foreign lands were still forbidden, and the government dispatched ships to trade; on return, fine goods paid two parts in ten, coarse goods two parts in fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 1 (1314), Maritime Trade Intendant Offices were re-established; private voyages abroad remained forbidden while the state sent its own ships; on return, fine goods paid two-tenths and coarse goods two-fifteenths.

sentences.zh: 七年，以下蕃之人將絲銀細物易於外國，又並提舉司罷之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, because people going to foreign lands were trading silk, silver, and fine goods overseas, the Intendant Office was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, because private traders were exchanging silk, silver, and fine goods abroad, the Intendant Office was abolished again.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，復立泉州、慶元、廣東三處提舉司，申嚴市舶之禁。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi, Intendant Offices at Quanzhou, Qingyuan, and Guangdong were re-established, and maritime trade prohibitions were strictly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizhi 2 (1322), Intendant Offices at Quanzhou, Qingyuan, and Guangdong were re-established and maritime trade restrictions were strictly enforced.

sentences.zh: 三年，聽海商貿易，歸征其稅。

translations.literal: In the third year, maritime merchants were permitted to trade, and taxes were levied upon their return.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, maritime merchants were allowed to trade freely, with taxes collected on their return.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，諸海舶至者，止令行省抽分。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding, all arriving merchant ships were ordered to be proportionally taxed only by branch secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiding 1 (1324), arriving merchant ships were to be taxed by branch secretariats alone.

sentences.zh: 其大略如此。

translations.literal: The broad pattern was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the general pattern.

sentences.zh: 若夫中買寶貨之制，泰定三年命省臣依累朝呈獻例給價。

translations.literal: As for the system of purchasing tribute goods at fixed prices, in the third year of Taiding provincial officials were ordered to pay prices according to the accumulated dynastic precedent for presenting tribute.
translations.idiomatic: As for the system of purchasing tribute goods at fixed prices, in Taiding 3 (1326) provincial officials were ordered to pay according to accumulated dynastic precedent for presented tribute.

sentences.zh: 天歷元年，以其蠹耗國財，詔加禁止，凡中獻者以違制論云。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianli, because this depleted state finances, an edict intensified the prohibition; all who presented goods for purchase were prosecuted for violating regulations.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianli 1 (1328), because the practice drained state finances, an edict tightened the ban; anyone presenting goods for purchase was prosecuted for violating regulations.
